The BioGENEius Challenge is the premier international competition hosted by the Biotechnology Institute that recognizes high school students (grades 9–12) for original, ground-breaking research in biotechnology. 
Students compete in one of three core categories focused on real-world biotechnology applications:
• Global Healthcare Challenge: Medical biotechnology, human health outcomes, diagnostics, and therapeutics.
• Global Sustainability Challenge: Agricultural biotechnology, crop, and animal applications.
• Global Environment Challenge: Industrial and environmental biotechnology, bioremediation, and biofuels.
Evaluation_Criteria: Biotech innovation, experimental design, potential industry application, Aspiring biological scientist conducting laboratory research with direct clinical or environmental utility

Name: International Sustainable World Project Olympiad (I-SWEEEP)
Description: International science fair focused on ground-breaking energy, engineering, and environmental solutions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Innovation, environmental relevance, scientific methodology, poster defense, Student environmental engineer who has created functional prototypes for renewable energy

Name: The Big Bang UK Young Scientists Competition
Description:
The Big Bang Fair is the UK's biggest annual STEM event for young people. Every year, thousands of young people attend The Big Bang Fair to take part in hands-on activities, careers panels and see incredible live shows. Students get the opportunity to hear first-hand from exciting scientists and engineers and connect with inspiring career role models. The Big Bang Competition rewards young people’s science, engineering and technology project work and crowns the UK Young Engineer, UK Young Scientist of the Year and UK Young Technologist of the Year, supported by Siemens. 
From a portable pollution monitor and revolutionising solar power, to investigating medical chemistry, the science, engineering and technology projects from today’s young talent are incredible.
Previous winners have gone on to represent the UK in international competitions, to study STEM at the highest levels, to work in some of our biggest engineering companies and to set up their own businesses.
Evaluation_Criteria: STEM approach, project planning, communication, real-world relevance, UK school student with an inventive science or engineering project tested through experiments, ,

Name: The Singapore Science and Engineering Fair
Description:
The Singapore Science & Engineering Fair (SSEF) is a national competition organised by the Ministry of Education (MOE), Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), and Science Centre Singapore (SCS). The SSEF is affiliated to the prestigious International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF), which is regarded as the Olympics of science competitions.
SSEF is an excellent platform for our budding scientists and engineers to showcase their passion by communicating their findings to industry experts. Selected winners will get to represent Singapore and compete at the ISEF.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific approach, experimental thoroughness, technical understanding, Top Singaporean student researcher working with A*STAR or university research mentors, ,

Name: Initiative for Research and Innovation in STEM (IRIS)
Description: The Initiative for Research and Innovation in STEM (IRIS) is India’s premier national pre-collegiate science competition. It nurtures scientific research and innovation among young school students, serving as the official pathway for Indian finalists to represent Team India at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) in the United States.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty of research, scientific methodology, experimental data, oral presentation, Top student researcher in India who has conducted lab-verified original science experiments, ,

Name: Tidewater Science and Engineering Fair
Description: The Tidewater Science Congress hosts the annual Tidewater Science and Engineering Fair (TSEF) for middle and high school students in the Hampton Roads region of Virginia.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific method, poster clarity, student understanding of research area, Regional high school researcher aiming to qualify for state and international science competitions, ,

Name: BIEA International STEM Competition
Description: The BIEA International STEM Youth Innovation Competition is an annual global science and engineering challenge hosted by the British International Education Association. The 2027 season is currently underway with the theme "Ocean Balance, Innovating to End Overfishing".
Evaluation_Criteria: Engineering design, ecological problem solving, report writing, presentation, Team of students eager to design technological solutions (drones, robotics) for wildlife conservation, ,

Name: EUROINVENT Creativity & Innovation
Description: The EUROINVENT Official Website is the main hub for the European Exhibition of Creativity and Innovation, one of the largest annual innovation and research events in Eastern Europe. It is organised by Romanian Inventors Forum (FIR), Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iași, and Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași, under the aegis of IFIA and WIIPA. EUROINVENT brings together over 690 inventions and projects from more than 30 to 45 countries across four primary tracks.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty, industrial applicability, prototype execution, patent potential, Student inventor with a functional prototype or patent application seeking global exhibition,

Name: Imperial College Schools Science Competition
Description: The Imperial College Science and Innovation Competition (run by the Faculty of Natural Sciences at Imperial College London) is a global STEM and problem-solving competition for young people. Teams create a 5-minute video pitch proposing an innovative scientific or technological solution linked to one or more of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Evaluation_Criteria: Creativity, scientific accuracy, communication engagement, teamwork, Young science communicator capable of explaining real scientific solutions in an engaging video, ,

Name: Fitzwilliam College Cambridge Economics Essay Prize
Description: The Fitzwilliam College Cambridge Economics Essay Competition is an annual writing contest for high school students in their penultimate year of education, offering a £200 first prize and a £25 runner-up book voucher.
Evaluation_Criteria: Economic analysis, independent evaluation, persuasive clarity, scholarship, Ambitious high school economist preparing for rigorous Oxbridge undergraduate study, ,

Name: Gould Prize for Essays in English Literature
Description:
Trinity College launched the Gould Prize for Essays in English Literature in 2013. This is an annual competition for Year 12 or Lower 6th students. The Prize has been established from a bequest made by Dr Dennis Gould in 2004 for the furtherance of education in English Literature. This Essay Prize has the following aims. First, to encourage talented students with an interest in English Literature to explore their reading interests further in response to questions about the subject. Second, to encourage students with an interest in literature to apply for a University course in English. Finally, to recognise the achievements of high-calibre students from whatever background they may come, as well as the achievements of those who teach them.
Candidates are invited each year to submit an essay of between 1,500 and 2,500 words in answer to a question from our list.  The word count excludes footnotes and references. Any widely used referencing style is acceptable as long as you use it consistently.
Candidates must write their essays entirely on their own: that is, without help from their school or from artificial intelligence. Your essay should represent your most ambitious, original, and imaginative critical work. We are not looking for submissions in creative writing. We also expect a close engagement with the prompt. Essays can be written on all works of literature composed originally in the English language, from anywhere in the world. Also eligible are all works of literature originally written in the British Isles in any other language (e.g. Welsh, Scottish Gaelic, Scots, Irish, French, Latin, Greek, etc). Excluded are works from beyond the British Isles that were not originally written in English (e.g. Leo Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina).
Evaluation_Criteria: Literary insight, analytical independence, depth of reading, close textual scrutiny, Perceptive reader capable of sophisticated literary criticism and historical context analysis, ,

Name: High School Academic Research Competition (SARC)
Description:
The High School Academic Research Competition is where talented students from around the world compete to present high-quality research on any topic. SARC challenges students to sharpen their critical thinking skills, immerse themselves in the research process, and hone their writing skills for success.
The competition is hosted completely online, breaking down geographical barriers and providing students from all over the world access to explore and develop their research interests.
Evaluation_Criteria: Research methodology, academic paper structure, clarity of contribution, Secondary student who has completed an academic paper seeking review from university researchers, ,

Name: IEA Monetary Policy Essay Prize
Description:
The IEA is the UK’s original free-market think-tank, founded in 1955. Our mission is to improve understanding of the fundamental institutions of a free society by analysing and expounding the role of markets in solving economic and social problems. As part of this, the IEA runs an extensive student outreach programme including internships, summer schools, seminars, and competitions. The IEA is an educational charity (No CC 235 351) and independent research institute limited by guarantee. Ideas and policies produced by the Institute are freely available from our website. The Institute is entirely independent of any political party or group, and is entirely funded by voluntary donations from individuals, companies, and foundations.
The purpose of the Institute of International Monetary Research is to demonstrate and bring to public attention the strong relationship between the quantity of money on the one hand, and the levels of national income and expenditure on the other. The Institute – which is associated with the University of Buckingham in England – was set up in 2014, in the aftermath of the Great Financial Crisis (a.k.a., “the Great Recession”) of 2007 – 2009. It is an educational charity.
Evaluation_Criteria: Monetary economic theory, empirical data use, analytical clarity, Student studying economics with an interest in central banking, inflation, and interest rate policy, ,

Name: Jane Austen Society of North America (JASNA) Contest
Description:
The Jane Austen Society of North America (JASNA) Essay Contest is an annual international writing competition that awards scholarships to students for analytical essays on Jane Austen’s works. Membership in JASNA is not required, and there is no entry fee.
Nine winners (first, second, and third place in each of the three divisions) are selected annually. Every winner receives a one-year JASNA membership, publication of their essay on the JASNA Website, and a set of Norton Critical Editions of Jane Austen’s novels.
Evaluation_Criteria: Textual knowledge of Austen's works, analytical insight, graceful writing, Literature student who appreciates 19th-century British literature and character dynamics

Name: Languages and Culture Essay Prize (Trinity Cambridge)
Description:
The Languages and Cultures Essay Prize is a competition that can be entered by students in Year 12 or the Lower 6th. Candidates are invited to submit an essay on one of a number of topics.
The essay should treat elements of any language (including English) and/or cultural form or artefact (literature, visual art, cinema, material culture, etc). Essays can be up to 3,000 words, including all footnotes and references but excluding the bibliography. Any widely used referencing style is acceptable as long as you use it consistently. It’s worth considering the use of examples in your essays: the best essays often use a diverse selection of contemporary, historical or literary examples.  We encourage you to provide references to your sources of information, and to include a bibliography at the end of the essay.
Evaluation_Criteria: Cross-cultural insight, linguistic nuance, critical evaluation of texts, Linguistically curious student preparing for modern language or comparative literature degrees

Name: LSE SU Economics Society Essay Competition
Description:
The LSESU Economics Society Essay Competition is a global academic event officially hosted by the LSESU Economics Society, tailored for outstanding high school students. All essay prompts are set by current professors in the LSE Department of Economics.
Past question setters include leading scholars: Professor Sir Christopher Pissarides (2010 Nobel Laureate in Economics), Professor Sir Tim Besley (former President of the Royal Economic Society), and Professor Sir Richard Layard (LSE Emeritus Professor, founder of happiness economics). Since its launch in 2017, the competition has drawn participants from over 60 countries and regions worldwide. Widely regarded as one of the most prestigious economics writing activities among UK high schools, it offers dual certification from LSE professors and the Economics Society for outstanding submissions. Awards serve as strong academic evidence for applications to economics programmes at top universities globally, marking a key step toward entering the world's leading economics institutions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Economic rigor, originality of argument, real-world empirical examples, Economics student able to craft well-researched arguments on contemporary economic shocks, ,

Name: Robert Walker Prize for Essays in Law
Description:
Trinity College was pleased to launch the Robert Walker Prize for Essays in Law in 2013. The prize is named after the Rt Hon. The Lord Walker of Gestingthorpe GBS PC (1938–2023), a judicial member of the House of Lords from 2002 and Justice of the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom from its creation in 2009 until his retirement in 2013. Lord Walker read law at Trinity, and became an Honorary Fellow of the College in 2006. He was a generous and dedicated supporter of Law at Trinity, meeting current and prospective students at College events, judging moots (legal debates) and helping to connect the practice of law with its academic study.
The Robert Walker Prize has three objectives: to encourage students with an interest in Law to explore that interest by researching, considering and developing an argument about a legal topic of importance to modern society, to encourage those interested in Law to apply for a university course in Law; and to recognise the achievements of high-calibre students, from whatever background they may come.
Evaluation_Criteria: Legal reasoning, analysis of precedent, ethical clarity, structure, Analytical thinker exploring the philosophy of jurisprudence and legal statutes, ,

Name: Royal Geographical Society School Essay Competition
Description: The Royal Geographical Society (with IBG) School Essay Competition is an annual writing contest run in partnership with the Financial Times (FT) for senior school students. It requires a clear, well-evidenced essay or an interactive ArcGIS StoryMap (maximum 1,000 words excluding title and references)
Evaluation_Criteria: Geographical thinking, data integration, spatial analysis, persuasive prose, Geography or social studies student interested in urban planning, climate migration, and resources

Name: Julia Wood Prize (History) St Hugh's Oxford
Description: The Julia Wood History Essay Prize is an annual history essay competition run by St Hugh's College, University of Oxford. The concluded 2026 rules accepted Sixth Form-equivalent students internationally and eligible gap-year students who had not progressed beyond that level. Students write an original historical essay of 2,000-4,000 words on a topic of their own choosing. The competition values original, enterprising topics and independent historical thinking; standard homework essays are unlikely to succeed. Up to £600 in prize money is awarded, often split between multiple candidates, with commendations given to further strong entries.
Evaluation_Criteria: Original historical argument, primary source scrutiny, historiographical awareness, History student with an appetite for independent archival research and academic writing, ,

Name: Mary Renault Prize (Classics) St Hugh's Oxford
Description: The Mary Renault Classical Reception Essay Competition is run annually by St Hugh's College, Oxford. Students write 2,000–4,000 word essays on the reception or influence of classical antiquity — ancient Greece, Rome, or related civilisations — in any discipline, including literature, history, art, film, or music. It includes wo or more prizes of up to £300 each, highly commended entries, and a September college invitation. The brief is open enough that you can argue about something you already care about, whether that's Sartre, a musical or a Victorian novel, and the published winning essays show you exactly the standard you're aiming for.
Evaluation_Criteria: Appreciation of classical literature, analytical depth, prose style, Classicist or humanities student exploring Greek and Roman history and literature, ,

Name: Yale International Relations Global Essay Competition
Description:
The Yale International Relations Association Global Essay Competition offers a unique opportunity for students to present their ideas and perspectives on global issues to Yale students and receive thoughtful feedback from peers accomplished in International Relations.
The competition encourages participants to think critically, explore complex global challenges, and experiment with diverse writing styles. With students participating from across the world, it fosters global dialogue while strengthening analytical and persuasive writing skills.
Students must submit a 400-word essay on the given theme. The theme will be announced in January 2027. Strong essays will clearly justify the chosen global issue and propose concise ideas for potential solutions. Finalist essays will be evaluated by Yale students, who will select the top three most inspiring submissions. Winning essays should challenge perspectives, demonstrate originality, and inspire reflection and action.
Evaluation_Criteria: Geopolitical analysis, policy feasibility, structural clarity, research citations, Student interested in foreign affairs, international security, and diplomatic history

Name: Woolf Essay Prize (Newnham College Cambridge)
Description: In 1928, Virginia Woolf addressed the Newnham Arts Society on the Subject of ‘Women and Fiction’, and from this talk emerged her seminal text, A Room of One’s Own. Newnham is very proud of its place in the history of women’s education, and we are delighted in the continuation of the Woolf Essay Prize. A Room of One’s Own raises a number of questions surrounding the place of women in society, culture, and education, and the competition allows students to contemplate these themes and ideas while developing the independent research and writing skills essential to university-level study.
Evaluation_Criteria: Intellectual curiosity, structural elegance, independent analysis of prompts, Ambitious female humanities student seeking to demonstrate academic readiness for Oxbridge, ,

Name: Cambridge Society for Economic Pluralism Contest
Description: The Cambridge Society for Economic Pluralism (CSEP) hosts an annual international essay competition for Sixth Form and high school students to explore alternative and interdisciplinary economic ideas beyond standard neoliberal syllabi. The word Count is 1,500 – 2,500 words (excluding citations), with Harvard referencing preferred. Generative AI is strictly restricted to ideation or refinement, must be explicitly declared, and cannot be used to write the actual text.
Evaluation_Criteria: Pluralist economic understanding, critical thinking beyond orthodox models
Ideal_Candidate: Student economist eager to challenge conventional textbook economic models with alternative theories

Name: CEMC Canadian Team Mathematics Contest
Description:
The Canadian Team Mathematics Contest (CTMC) is an exciting and challenging competition where participants work in teams to showcase their mathematical problem-solving skills through fun and engaging activities. A special feature of the CTMC is that schools can host the contest at their own school or be selected to participate at the University of Waterloo. 
The CEMC enables students to challenge themselves and build confidence. Students thrive in the collaborative format of the Canadian Team Mathematics Contest (CTMC) event. Contest preparation provides opportunities to network and form lasting friendships.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical ingenuity, multi-step problem solving, team synchronization, Mathematics team trained in Olympiad-style geometry, algebra, and number theory, ,

Name: Yale DHSRI High School Investment Competition
Description:
The Yale DHSRI High School Investment Competition is a virtual finance and investment challenge organized by the Dwight Hall Socially Responsible Investment Fund (DHSRI) at Yale University. 
Form a solid team with dedicated and knowledgeable members. It's essential for everyone to work together, share ideas, and divide tasks effectively. Each team member should contribute to the decision-making and research process.
One key to success in this competition is conducting thorough research on the stocks you choose to invest in. Understand the industries, the company's competitive position, financial statements, and growth potential. Following trusted financial news sources and seeking advice from investment professionals can also be beneficial.
A well-diversified portfolio is crucial in any investment context, including the Yale DHSRI competition. Make sure to spread your investments across multiple sectors and industries to minimize risk and maximize potential returns.
Concentrate on the long-term performance of your investments rather than chasing short-term market fluctuations. The competition rewards teams with a consistent track record of strong investment decisions, so avoid speculating or making impulsive moves.
Pay attention to your mid-year and final presentations, as well as your team's written reports. Communicating your investment strategy clearly and professionally is vital for success in the competition. Ensure that your presentations cover your portfolio's performance, analytical methods, decision-making process, and the rationale for your specific investment choices.
Evaluation_Criteria: Financial modeling depth, risk-reward analysis, moat identification, Student investor capable of building three-statement valuation models and equity theses, ,

Name: Global Youth Entrepreneurship Challenge (GYEC)
Description:
The Global Youth Entrepreneurship Challenge (GYEC) is an online 12-hour business idea competition for high school students. You can participate from anywhere as long as you have internet access. The GYEC inspires young people to develop an entrepreneurial mindset while enhancing their understanding of business and innovation. It challenges high school students worldwide to tackle pressing global issues through innovative and sustainable business ideas. Additionally, participants learn to apply their knowledge of science and technology in a practical way.
To register for the competition, participants must form a team of 3 to 8 eligible students, ideally combining a diverse range of skills in science, technology, business, marketing, and communication. The competition journey begins with the selection of team members. To qualify for the global finals, teams must first win the preliminary round and earn a place as their country’s representative team. In both stages, teams of 3 to 8 high school students compete to solve a given challenge within 12 hours.
Evaluation_Criteria: Rapid business ideation, team collaboration, financial forecasting, video pitch, Entrepreneurial team capable of formulating and packaging a complete business plan in half a day, ,

Name: UT Dallas Top Trader Stock Market Competition
Description:
The UT Dallas Top Trader Stock Market Competition is an annual summer virtual investing challenge hosted by the Naveen Jindal School of Management at The University of Texas at Dallas. It introduces high school students to investment management, personal finance, and portfolio strategy using a simulated trading platform. 
Each student starts with $1,000,000 in virtual cash to invest in U.S. stocks and ETFs. The entire contest runs online, so students can compete from anywhere without traveling to campus. Alongside trading, participants access instructional videos and quizzes created by UT Dallas finance faculty and staff. Completing these modules allows students to earn Investment and Personal Finance Knowledge certificates.
Evaluation_Criteria: Total trading performance, portfolio diversification, risk metrics, High school student interested in personal finance, equity screening, and portfolio analysis, ,

Name: Ithaca College High School Investment Competition
Description:
The High School Investment Competition brings real-world investment tactics into the classroom. Ithaca College School of Business invites high school teams in the northeast to compete in Annual Investment Competition where students will learn basic principles of the stock market, various sectors, and fundamentals of real-time trading, with the opportunity to win great prizes!
Teams composed of 3-6 student members ranging from 9th to 12th grades will receive $1,000,000 in virtual US dollars and will build a portfolio that consists of five to twenty stocks! At the conclusion of the competition, awards will be given out to the top three earning portfolios.
Evaluation_Criteria: Portfolio return, adherence to asset allocation, investment report, Team interested in learning fund management, asset allocation, and market analysis, ,

Name: TCU High School Investor Challenge
Description:
This program for high-achieving high school seniors brings you to campus for a week of training in securities analysis before managing a $100,000 virtual stock portfolio. Offered by the LKCM Center for Financial Studies at TCU Neeley School of Business.
Spend five days living on campus and taking college-level finance classes at the TCU Neeley School of Business. You’ll study securities analysis and portfolio management, learning how to evaluate companies and build investment strategies using real-world data.
You’ll apply what you’ve learned by managing a virtual portfolio throughout your senior year, submitting periodic stock reports for feedback and refinement.
Evaluation_Criteria: Fundamental analysis, portfolio management, stock presentation, Student seeking foundational knowledge in corporate finance and portfolio valuation, ,

Name: Bentley University Summer Stock Market Challenge
Description:
The Bentley University Summer Stock Market Challenge is a free, month-long virtual investing competition hosted by Bentley University for U.S. high school students. Participants manage a simulated portfolio of $50,000 in virtual currency on the StockTrak platform to compete for cash gift card prizes.
Students trade real-time U.S. stocks, ETFs, and other securities using $50,000 in virtual funds via the Bentley University Investment Challenge portal. The platform also provides streaming rankings, analyst ratings, and introductory trading tutorials.
Evaluation_Criteria: Simulated capital returns, risk-adjusted portfolio growth, trade log, Student eager to experience trading floor terminals, Bloomberg interfaces, and financial data, ,

Name: National Personal Finance Challenge
Description:
The National Personal Finance Challenge (NPFC), run by the Council for Economic Education, is a nationwide high school competition designed to test and build students' money management, investing, and financial planning skills.  Teams start with an online qualifying exam (typically a 30-question test) covering personal finance domains. State champions advance to the national finals. 
It involves two phases:
Case Study Round: Teams analyze a complex, hypothetical family financial scenario under a tight time limit and present their comprehensive plan to a panel of judges; the top 16 teams advance.
Quiz Bowl Round: A fast-paced, Jeopardy-style quiz bowl tests live knowledge on topics like retirement accounts, bonds (such as TIPS), insurance, and mortgages, narrowing down to the top 4 teams and eventually crowning a national champion.
Evaluation_Criteria: Knowledge of consumer finance, investing, debt, and rapid-fire quiz buzzer rounds, Team of students well-versed in personal financial planning, tax brackets, and insurance

Name: Capitol Hill Challenge (SIFMA Foundation)
Description:
The Capitol Hill Challenge (CHC) is a national financial and civics education competition organized by the SIFMA Foundation and underwritten by the Charles Schwab Foundation. Launched in 2004, the free annual program pairs public middle and high school students with their local Members of Congress while they compete in an online investment simulation. 
Teams use The Stock Market Game to manage a hypothetical $100,000 portfolio over roughly 14 weeks each spring. Students invest in real-time across stocks, bonds, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and impact investments.
Evaluation_Criteria: Portfolio value, asset diversification, financial literacy quiz scores, Public school economics class managing a virtual investment portfolio over 14 weeks, ,

Name: Bennington College Young Writers Awards
Description:
The Bennington College Young Writers Awards celebrate exceptional high school students in grades 9-12 whose writing demonstrates originality, curiosity, craft, and creative ambition. 
For two decades, the Bennington Young Writers Awards have recognized outstanding writing by high school students from around the world. Now part of the Bennington Young Creators Awards, this long-running program continues to honor poetry, fiction, and nonfiction by the next generation of literary voices.
Open to students worldwide, these awards are free to enter and offer cash prizes up to $2,000, recognition, publication, or showcase opportunities, and scholarships for students who enroll at Bennington College. All submissions to the Young Writers Awards will be reviewed for authenticity and originality. No Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used to brainstorm, create, draft, revise, or collaborate in any way. Submissions that utilize AI will be disqualified. Submissions that utilize AI will only be considered for the Young Innovators Awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Original narrative voice, emotional honesty, literary command, Aspiring novelist, poet, or personal essayist with distinct imaginative language

Name: Write the World Monthly Competitions
Description: Write the World's free monthly competitions for teen writers (ages 13-19) offer opportunities to explore a variety of exciting genres, from poetry, fantasy, and flash fiction to environmental writing and journalism. Young writers of all levels are welcome to join our vibrant community and share their work with peers from around the globe who are eager to read their words.
Evaluation_Criteria: Peer review participation, writing craft, revision effort, prompt adherence
Ideal_Candidate: Young writer looking for an encouraging community to hone writing craft monthly

Name: YoungArts National Arts Competition
Description:
For many young people, applying to YoungArts may be the first step in affirming “I am an artist.” YoungArts is one of the only organizations in the U.S. that supports artists across 10 disciplines at all stages of development, beginning with the critical moment when they decide to pursue a life in the arts, and continuing throughout their careers. 
Artists ages 15–18, or grades 10–12, in the U.S. are encouraged to apply in the discipline of their choice. All applications are evaluated by esteemed discipline-specific panels of artists through an adjudication process that includes multiple rounds of review. Award winners are offered a lifetime of artistic support and ongoing connection with an extraordinarily robust network of peers and mentors.
Evaluation_Criteria: Artistic excellence, portfolio depth, exceptional creative promise, Pre-professional teen creative writer with a cohesive portfolio of poetry, fiction, or nonfiction

Name: The Alpine Fellowship Youth Writing Prize
Description: The Alpine Fellowship Writing Prize is an international literary competition hosted annually by The Alpine Fellowship, a charitable foundation that supports and showcases emerging artists, writers, and academics. Participants must submit original, unpublished prose (fiction, non-fiction, or non-academic essay) typically up to 2,500 words (though specific word limits can adjust per yearly guidelines).
Evaluation_Criteria: Philosophical depth, original literary voice, thematic maturity, Reflective writer who can craft literary fiction or essays around broad humanistic themes, ,

Name: One Teen Story Contest
Description: The One Teen Story Contest is a global short-fiction writing competition hosted by the literary arts nonprofit One Story. It invites young writers to submit original stories exploring the teen experience for a cash prize and professional publication. Each winner receives $500, individual editorial work with a One Teen Story editor, and publication on the One Story Website.
Evaluation_Criteria: Narrative momentum, authentic character dialogue, emotional arc, Teen fiction writer who can write complete, moving 3000-word stories about youth life, ,

Name: Immerse Education Essay Competition
Description: The Immerse Education Essay Competition gives students aged 13–18 the chance to submit an essay on a question that sparks their interest. Each year, we refresh our list of questions to encourage students to explore their favourite subjects in greater depth. With more than twenty options available in our Essay Competition Guide, there’s plenty to choose from. Up to ten winners will receive a full scholarship to study with us at a world-leading university of their choice, and outstanding runners-up will also be awarded partial scholarships.
Evaluation_Criteria: Intellectual curiosity, structural reasoning, research depth on prompt, Motivated student seeking academic summer enrichment in law, medicine, or engineering

Name: Stephen Spender Prize
Description: The Stephen Spender Prize is a leading annual poetry in translation competition in the UK and Ireland, organized by the Stephen Spender Trust to celebrate multilingualism, literary creativity, and the art of translation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Poetic translation fidelity, commentary on linguistic choices, creativity, Bilingual student who can translate world poetry into rich, metered English verse,

Name: Nancy Thorp Poetry Award
Description:
Sponsored by Hollins University, the Nancy Thorp Poetry Contest provides scholarships, prizes, and recognition for the best poems submitted by young women in their sophomore or junior year of high school.
At Hollins, you’ll join a new generation of authors in growing your craft and fostering a way of seeing and saying that is distinctively your own. With our multi-genre approach, you’ll develop a working knowledge in poetry, fiction, and nonfiction that’s intertwined with the study of literature. And, you’ll be immersed in a diversity of writers, writing theories, and literary experiences on campus, led by a faculty whose publishing success surpasses that of any other liberal arts college.
Evaluation_Criteria: Poetic voice, emotional clarity, formal technique, Female teen poet looking to pursue creative writing at the university level, ,

Name: Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize for Young Writers
Description:
The Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize for Young Writers, created in 2007 to recognize outstanding young poets, is an annual contest for poets who are sophomores and juniors in high school. The contest is named in honor of Patricia Grodd in recognition of her generous support of The Kenyon Review and its programs, as well as her passionate commitment to education and deep love for poetry.
The poems by the winner and runners-up will be published in The Kenyon Review, and the winner receives a full scholarship to a Kenyon Review Young Writers workshop. Submissions for the contest are open every year November 1 through November 30.
Evaluation_Criteria: Literary excellence, fresh sensory imagery, rhythmic discipline, Serious young poet whose writing shows exceptional aesthetic maturity,

Name: Rattle Poetry Prize (Young Poets Category)
Description:
The annual Rattle Poetry Prize offers $15,000 for a single poem to be published in the winter issue of the magazine. Ten finalists will also receive $500 each and publication, and be eligible for the $5,000 Readers’ Choice Award, to be selected by subscriber and entrant vote.
Additional poems from the entries are frequently offered publication as well. In 2025 we published 28 poems that had been submitted to the contest from over 6,000 entries.
With the winners judged in an anonymized review by the editors to ensure a fair and consistent selection, an entry fee that is simply a one-year subscription to the magazine—and a large Readers’ Choice Award to be chosen by the writers themselves—we’ve designed the Rattle Poetry Prize to be one of the most inspiring contests around.
Past winners have included a retired teacher, a lawyer, and several students. It’s fair, it’s friendly, and you win a print subscription to Rattle even if you don’t win.
Evaluation_Criteria: Originality, poetic rhythm, authenticity of teenage experience, Poet writing unflinching, honest, and technically accomplished verse, ,

Name: Princeton University Ten-Minute Play Contest
Description: The Princeton University Ten-Minute Play Contest is an annual playwriting competition hosted by the Lewis Center for the Arts and the Program in Theater at Princeton University. It recognizes outstanding dramatic writing by high school juniors worldwide. Submissions must be original, English-language plays strictly limited to 10 pages (or 10 minutes in performance length).
Evaluation_Criteria: Dramatic tension, dialogue realism, theatrical staging feasibility, High school playwright who can establish character conflict within ten compact pages, ,

Name: Youth for Human Rights International (YHRI) Essay Competition
Description: The Youth for Human Rights International (YHRI) Essay Competition is an annual global writing contest inviting young people aged 18 and under to share their perspectives on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Winning entries are announced on Human Rights Day (December 10) and featured on the official website. Ground your essay in specific articles from the Universal Declaration of Human Rights rather than speaking only in general terms, share how human rights impact your local community, school, or personal experiences to make your piece stand out & stick closely to the one-page limit by focusing on one clear message or a specific right that resonates most with you.
Evaluation_Criteria: Human rights analysis, international law awareness, moral clarity, Advocate passionate about the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and legal equity, ,

Name: NSHSS Creative Writing Scholarship
Description:
The NSHSS Creative Writing Scholarship is an annual merit-based award offered by the National Society of High School Scholars (NSHSS) to recognize high school student writers. It awards $2,000 to select winners in creative writing categories, with recent cycles splitting poetry and fiction into distinct tracks.
Historically, the NSHSS Creative Writing Scholarship has awarded six $2,000 prizes total, split evenly between Fiction and Poetry. In the 2026 cycle, NSHSS also began listing dedicated genre awards, such as the NSHSS Poetry Scholarship, offering two $2,000 awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creativity, narrative structure, expressive use of language, Student member of NSHSS with strong creative expression in fiction or poetry, ,

Name: NCERT National Story Writing Competition
Description: Rashtriya Ekta Divas (National Unity Day) is observed every year on 31stOctober to commemorate Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary. It not only commemorates the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of national integration of independent India, but also re-affirms the inherent strength and resilience of our nation to withstand threats to the unity, integrity and security of the Country. National Unity Day this year will follow the theme of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav. Accordingly, a national level Story Writing competition on the theme – "the contribution of paired State/Union Territory (UT) in India's Struggle for Freedom" is being launched by the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India. The competition aims to explore students' creative instincts and encourage them to write about the contributions of their paired states to India's struggle for freedom in accordance with the Ek Bharat Shrestha Bharat (EBSB) matrix.
Evaluation_Criteria: Literary expression, regional cultural values, narrative imagination, Indian school student who writes engaging literary fiction in English, Hindi, or regional tongues, ,

Name: NLSIU Consumer Rights Day Essay Competition
Description: The Chair on Consumer Law and Practice (CLAP) at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru organizes an annual National Essay Competition to commemorate National Consumer Day (December 24). The competition is open to students, academics, professionals, government officials, consumer advocates, and anyone interested in consumer protection. First place receives ₹10,000 and a Certificate of Merit. Winners are felicitated on National Consumer Day, and selected entries may be published in the CLAP Newsletter.
Evaluation_Criteria: Consumer law reasoning, statutory analysis, policy critique, Indian pre-law student interested in consumer protection legislation and regulatory economics,

Name: CBSE Expression Series
Description: The CBSE Expression Series is a national-level online and offline competition organized by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) for students from classes 1 to 12.  Students can express their creativity through essays, paragraphs, poems, or paintings, written/drawn in English or any of the 22 scheduled Indian languages. Schools conduct internal rounds, shortlist top entries per category, and submit them digitally through the official CBSE Expression Series App available on the Google Play Store.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creative expression, thematic adherence, clarity of message, Indian student in CBSE curriculum who excels in prompt-based essays and patriotic tributes, ,

Name: PCRA National Essay Competition
Description: The PCRA Competitions Portal hosts annual national-level essay writing, painting, and quiz competitions organized by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA) under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. The objective is to raise awareness among school children about fuel conservation, clean energy, and reducing carbon footprints. Features cash prizes at both state and national levels (with national essay winners typically receiving cash awards).
Evaluation_Criteria: Practical energy conservation strategies, clarity, linguistic correctness, Indian student who can propose practical, household and industrial petroleum saving methods, ,

Name: NHRC Youth Human Rights Essay Contest
Description: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India periodically conducts essay writing and youth-oriented competitions, such as its specific Hindi essay competitions for reserved categories (such as Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes) and annual human rights awareness activities, though specific ongoing youth essay contest portals and active calls vary by season.
Evaluation_Criteria: Constitutional awareness, analysis of civil liberties, persuasive solutions, Student who understands the Indian Constitution, fundamental rights, and social justice, ,

Name: National Young Authors Challenge
Description: The National Young Authors Challenge 2.0 (NYAC 2.0) is India’s nationwide short story writing competition for school students in Grades 5 to 12, presented by Big Red Education in partnership with Penguin Random House India. Top 50 Stories from each category (100 stories in total) will be compiled and published in two separate anthologies by Penguin Random House India. Next 100 Stories (50 from each category) will be officially featured and showcased on the Penguin India Official Website.
Evaluation_Criteria: Plot structure, character development, prose polish, book manuscript promise, Young Indian author who has drafted or wants to draft a full-length fiction manuscript, ,

Name: Keekli Pan-India Short Story Competition
Description:
The Keekli Pan-India Short Story Writing Competition is an annual national literary contest organized by the Shimla-based Keekli Charitable Trust for young writers across India. Designed to nurture emerging talent, the competition culminates in the publication of the top entries in a national anthology.
Participants can submit works on an open theme or draw inspiration from their city or state's folklore, monuments, history, and culture. Accepted genres include fiction, non-fiction, travelogue, and memoir.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creative storytelling, dialogue authenticity, pacing, Indian cultural setting, Young writer looking to get their short stories published in print anthologies, ,

Name: Story Glory National Contest
Description: There is no single event officially titled the "Story Glory National Contest." Instead, the name closely matches two distinct competitions: an international monthly short story contest called Story Glory and an Indian online talent competition called the Glitz & Glory National Championship, which features a dedicated storytelling category.
Evaluation_Criteria: Imaginative narrative, character warmth, moral theme, Elementary and middle school student developing storytelling confidence, ,

Name: Winged Words Student Writing Contest
Description:
If you are referring to the Wingword Poetry Prize (commonly searched as the Winged Words contest) organized by Delhi Poetry Slam, it is an annual nationwide online poetry competition in India open to students and adults.
Poems can be submitted in English, Hindi, or regional languages including Urdu, Punjabi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Odia, Assamese, and Gujarati. • Poems must be original works. Entries of any length, style, or subject are accepted, and no live performance is required.
Evaluation_Criteria: Linguistic flair, poetic rhythm, structural clarity, Student writer who enjoys playing with figurative language and emotional poetry, ,

Name: GEMA International Storywriting Competition
Description: Think you can write a winning story in 1,500 words or less? Enter GEMA International Short Story Writing Competition Today! If you are a writer aged 18 or younger - wanting to get published, Participate to get published in the Best story Book by and for Kids, distributed globally and win Trophies, Medals, Kidzania Passes, Training Programs and Certificates! in evening.
Evaluation_Criteria: Story arc, linguistic accuracy, originality of concept, School student developing writing fluency across diverse fictional prompts, ,

Name: India Writing Project (IWP)
Description: India Writing Project (IWP) is a dynamic platform fostering literary talent across the nation. We provide aspiring writers with opportunities to showcase their skills, receive recognition, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through our competitions, workshops, and publishing initiatives, we aim to nurture creativity and elevate Indian literature on the global stage.
Evaluation_Criteria: Writing under time pressure, plot twists, emotional engagement, Quick-witted writer who can create an engaging short story over a single weekend, ,

Name: Tata Building India School Essay Competition
Description: The Tata Building India School Essay Competition is one of India's largest annual youth essay-writing contests organized by the Tata Group. It aims to inspire school students to share visionary ideas for national development.
Evaluation_Criteria: Patriotic nation-building ideas, practical social solutions, expressive clarity, Indian school student who writes passionately about national development and civic values, ,

Name: WWF-India Wild Wisdom Challenge
Description: The WWF-India Wild Wisdom Global Challenge (WWGC) is the world's largest wildlife and nature quiz competition for school students. Launched by WWF-India in 2008, the 19th edition in 2026 carries the theme "From the Coastline to the Seafloor: An Ocean Odyssey" and focuses on marine ecosystems, underwater biodiversity, and ocean conservation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Ecological awareness, biodiversity knowledge, conservation solutions, Nature enthusiast who loves wildlife biology, forests, and environmental preservation, ,

Name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
Description: The CSIR Innovation Award for School Children (CIASC) is the primary national competition where students submit written innovation proposals, essays, or technical reports to the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR). Additionally, individual CSIR laboratories and headquarters host periodic thematic essay competitions (such as during Vigilance Awareness Week, National Science Day, or special commemorations).
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific problem solving, rural economic feasibility, reporting clarity, Student who has analyzed rural community dilemmas and proposed scientific fixes, ,

Name: INTACH Heritage Club Essay Competition
Description: The Young INTACH Activities and Announcements Page provides updates on heritage club competitions, including poster-making and essay-writing events organized by INTACH's Heritage Education and Communication Service (HECS). National winners are invited to Delhi for an immersive educational trip.
Evaluation_Criteria: Historical research of local heritage, architectural appreciation, conservation ideas, Student curious about ancient Indian monuments, traditional crafts, and oral history, ,

Name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Essay Competition
Description:
Babasaheb is known as one of the tallest reformers of India particularly in relation to providing social justice and empowerment to the weaker and depressed section of the population. It becomes imperative for the young Indians to get inspired by this versatile genius and creatively rediscover Babasaheb’s thoughts and ideology, which can be reflected from their writings in the form of essays.
Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF) was set up in pursuance of the recommendations of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s Centenary Celebrations Committee constituted under the Chairmanship of the then Prime Minister. One of the major objectives of DAF is to provide financial aid to the institutions propagating Babasaheb’s memory, organize a special campaign for removal of untouchability and caste based prejudices for bringing an attitudinal change in the society through communal harmony and brotherhood and to organize essay competitions, quiz competitions, lectures, seminars and symposia etc. on socio-economic issues to full the vision of Babasaheb to build an ideal society —a society based on social justice and equity— that gives permanency to the great achievements of modern Indian nation.
The primary objective of this Essay Competition is to encourage school, college and university students of 10 th and 12 th standards to write on the contribution of Babasaheb, particularly on his thoughts on social justice, empowerment of the depressed section, removal of caste-based discriminations like untouchability and atrocities on Dalits, national integration, communal harmony and the like.
The topics of the essay shall be selected every year by the respective Chairs from the themes based on Dr. Ambedkar’s thoughts on social justice, removal of inequality and discrimination, ameliorating the conditions of weaker sections of the society, removal of untouchability, caste-based prejudices, disparities, equality of opportunity, social democracy etc.
Evaluation_Criteria: Constitutional scholarship, social equity perspectives, historical knowledge, Humanities student reflecting on social equality, caste emancipation, and legal rights, ,

Name: Inter-DPS Society Regional Essay Competition
Description: The Inter-DPS Essay Writing Competition is an annual literary contest organized under the aegis of The Delhi Public School Society across its member schools. First launched in the 2025–26 academic session, the competition spans multiple rounds—beginning at the school/zonal level and culminating in a grand finale hosted at Delhi Public School, Vasant Kunj.
Evaluation_Criteria: Thematic originality, vocabulary, analytical structure, DPS student who excels in inter-school literary and debates competitions, ,

Name: Inte+A2:R24rnational Children's Peace Prize
Description: Awarded annually by the KidsRights Foundation to a young changemaker aged 12-17 who has achieved concrete, measurable impact advancing children's rights, offering the Nkosi statuette, education support, and a EUR 50,000 project grant.
Evaluation_Criteria: Documented history of fighting for children's rights, measurable local/national/global outcomes, third-party nomination, leadership courage
Ideal_Candidate: Young changemaker with an established independently verified record of advancing children's rights

Name: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award
Description: Founded in 1956 and operating across more than 130 countries, The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award is the world's leading non-competitive youth self-development framework. Participants progress through Bronze (14+), Silver (15+), and Gold (16+) levels over 6 to 18+ months by logging sustained goals via the Online Record Book across four core sections—Voluntary Service, Physical Recreation, Skills, and an Adventurous Journey—plus a 5-day Residential Project at the Gold level.
Evaluation_Criteria: Sustained multi-month commitment across Voluntary Service, Physical Recreation, Skills, and Adventurous Journey milestones
Ideal_Candidate: Self-motivated teen committed to structured personal growth, endurance, and long-term community service

Name: Glocal Teen Hero
Description: Initiated by Glocal Pvt. Ltd., Glocal Teen Hero is an annual regional recognition platform honoring exceptional teenagers aged 13–19 across South Asia (including Nepal, India, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh) who create meaningful social impact beyond academics. Applicants submit detailed documentation and essays on their initiatives, advancing through a Top 20 shortlist and Top 6 finalists round featuring live expert jury interviews and an awards ceremony celebrating youth innovation and leadership.
Evaluation_Criteria: Impact beyond academics, innovation, documented achievements, jury interview performance
Ideal_Candidate: South Asian teenager leading an active social, creative, or entrepreneurial community initiative

Name: Glocal Teen Hero India
Description: The Indian national edition of Glocal Teen Hero celebrates Indian teenagers aged 13–19 who drive measurable change in society through grassroots activism, social entrepreneurship, technology, or creative leadership. Candidates undergo multi-stage evaluation of their portfolio, project sustainability, and community outcomes, with Top 20 honorees and Top 6 finalists advancing to personal jury interviews for the national title.
Evaluation_Criteria: Community impact, innovation, supporting evidence/CV, personal jury interview
Ideal_Candidate: Indian teenager with verifiable grassroots leadership or social innovation work

Name: Three Dot Dash Global Teen Leaders (We Are Family Foundation)
Description: Hosted by the We Are Family Foundation, Three Dot Dash is a yearlong leadership and social-entrepreneurship accelerator selecting roughly 25–35 Global Teen Leaders aged 13–19 who are actively scaling initiatives addressing basic human needs or environmental sustainability. Selected leaders attend the all-expenses-paid Just Peace Summit (covering travel, accommodations, meals, and visas) and receive 1-on-1 expert mentorship, media training, and global network access.
Evaluation_Criteria: Active initiative (6+ months), tangible community/environmental impact, founder/key leader role, multi-year commitment
Ideal_Candidate: Teen founder or key leader scaling an established social or environmental impact organization

Name: Riley's Way Call for Kindness
Description: Organized by the Riley's Way Foundation, Call for Kindness is an annual fellowship and grant competition supporting U.S.-based youth leaders aged 13–23 (up to two co-leaders per project) whose initiatives strengthen communities through empathy and inclusion. Up to 45–50 winning teams receive up to $5,000 in two-tranche project funding alongside a yearlong Kind Leadership Curriculum featuring monthly virtual workshops, coaching, peer mentoring, and an in-person Leadership Summit.
Evaluation_Criteria: Kindness-centered community impact, project feasibility, inclusive collaborative leadership
Ideal_Candidate: Empathetic U.S. youth leader launching or scaling a community-building initiative

Name: Children's Climate Prize
Description: Founded in 2016 and administered by the Sweden-based Children's Climate Foundation, the Children's Climate Prize honors young innovators, activists, and organizations aged 12–17 worldwide whose projects or inventions deliver tangible climate and environmental impact. Finalists are evaluated by an international jury on scalability and measurable ecological outcomes, with winners invited to Stockholm to receive a medal, diploma, and SEK 100,000 to advance their work.
Evaluation_Criteria: Direct positive climate/environmental impact, innovation, project validation, scalability
Ideal_Candidate: Young climate innovator or activist aged 12-17 with a functioning eco-project or invention

Name: Peace First Grants
Description: Peace First supports young changemakers aged 13–25 globally who are launching grassroots projects tackling community injustices and root-cause social challenges. Teams complete Peace First's free, guided 5-step digital curriculum (Choose, Understand, Plan, Act, Reflect) to refine their action plan and pitch for mini-grants of up to $250, supplemented by peer feedback, mentor check-ins, and access to an international youth peacebuilding community.
Evaluation_Criteria: Compassion, courage, collaborative change, root-cause injustice analysis, feasible action plan
Ideal_Candidate: Youth organizer starting an early-stage grassroots project addressing social injustice

Name: The Pollination Project
Description: The Pollination Project is a global micro-granting foundation that awards seed grants of $500 to $1,000 every day of the year to grassroots, volunteer-led projects advancing environmental sustainability, compassion, and social justice. Geared toward early-stage charitable initiatives operating on total project budgets under $10,000, the program connects grantees with ongoing capacity-building resources and a worldwide alumni network.
Evaluation_Criteria: Grassroots community need, budget discipline (<$10k project budget), non-profit charitable purpose
Ideal_Candidate: Volunteer community organizer seeking initial seed capital for a charitable grassroots initiative

Name: Youth To The Front Fund
Description: An initiative of the We Are Family Foundation, the Youth To The Front Fund backs young activists, artists, filmmakers, and community organizers under 30 who confront systemic injustice, climate inequity, and marginalization through creative action and frontline organizing. Grantees receive up to $10,000 in direct project funding alongside strategic mentorship, storytelling support, and global platform visibility.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creative cultural impact, focus on marginalized communities, systemic change potential
Ideal_Candidate: Young artist, filmmaker, or creative organizer under 30 driving social justice through culture

Name: National Geographic Slingshot Challenge
Description: Created by the National Geographic Society with philanthropic partners, the Slingshot Challenge invites young people aged 13–18 worldwide (competing solo or in teams of up to six) to propose actionable solutions to environmental issues such as waste reduction, ocean restoration, clean air, and climate resilience. Participants submit a concise one-minute video pitch for the chance to earn up to $10,000 in funding and National Geographic recognition.
Evaluation_Criteria: Solution originality, alignment with challenge focus areas, 1-minute storytelling clarity, feasibility
Ideal_Candidate: Creative teen communicator pitching a focused, actionable local environmental solution

Name: Lead4Change Student Leadership Program
Description: Lead4Change is a free, educator-facilitated leadership curriculum and service-learning competition for middle and high school teams working with an adult sponsor. Students progress through structured leadership lessons to identify a community need, execute a measurable service project with peer and community partners, and submit a final project summary to compete for charity grants benefiting their partner organizations.
Evaluation_Criteria: Team collaboration, measurable community service outcomes, structured leadership application
Ideal_Candidate: School club or classroom team building a structured service project with teacher sponsorship

Name: Karma for Cara Microgrant Program
Description: Honoring the legacy of Cara Becker, the Karma for Cara Microgrant Program awards quarterly grants of $250 to $1,000 to U.S. students aged 18 and under to execute hands-on community service projects. Applications are reviewed following January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1 deadlines, prioritizing youth-led creativity, clear itemized budgets, and initiatives that mobilize peer volunteers.
Evaluation_Criteria: Youth-led creativity, tangible community benefit, peer volunteer involvement, budget clarity
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. K-12 student leading a localized volunteer or civic improvement project

Name: Awesome Foundation Grants
Description: The Awesome Foundation is a decentralized global network of more than 70 autonomous city and thematic chapters, each pooling member contributions to award monthly $1,000 no-strings-attached microgrants. Through a short, accessible application, teens, artists, builders, and community organizers can pitch bold, unconventional projects across technology, arts, science, and civic life for rapid chapter-level funding.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty, surprise and delight, feasibility with $1,000 seed funding, chapter alignment
Ideal_Candidate: Scrappy builder, artist, or teen organizer with a bold, unconventional $1,000 project idea

Name: Captain Planet Foundation (Planeteers)
Description: Through its Planeteer Alliance, the Captain Planet Foundation equips young environmental advocates aged 10–25 worldwide with structured training, virtual and in-person summits, and campaign toolkits to drive measurable ecological change. Active Planeteers collaborate across thematic climate campaigns and gain access to seed microgrants and mentorship to launch local conservation, decarbonization, and environmental justice projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Environmental stewardship, campaign mobilization, ecological or STEM action focus
Ideal_Candidate: Young eco-advocate aged 10-25 seeking mentorship and campaign funding for local climate action

Name: Global Changemakers Project Grants
Description: Global Changemakers is an international youth-empowerment organization that convenes Global Youth Summits and awards $1,000 seed grants to experienced young social entrepreneurs and activists aged 18–28. Applicants trained through its summits or programs pitch sustainable, community-validated initiatives via written proposals and video presentations to receive seed capital, capacity-building workshops, and peer support.
Evaluation_Criteria: Proven community leadership, project sustainability, video pitch, social impact track record
Ideal_Candidate: Experienced young social entrepreneur or activist seeking global summit networking and seed grants

Name: DoSomething.org Impact Scholarships & Grants
Description: DoSomething.org is one of the largest youth civic-action platforms in the United States and Canada, awarding more than $300,000 annually in scholarships to young people aged 13–25. Participants select monthly social-impact, voter-registration, mental-health, or environmental campaigns, complete real-world community actions, and submit verified photo or written reportbacks to qualify for scholarship drawings and impact grants.
Evaluation_Criteria: Verified campaign completion, civic engagement, photo/reportback submission
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. or Canadian teen seeking accessible civic-action campaigns with scholarship incentives

Name: Hershey Heartwarming Young Heroes GYSD Grants
Description: Administered by Youth Service America (YSA) with support from The Hershey Company, the Hershey Heartwarming Young Heroes program awards $250 to $1,000 grants to youth aged 5–25 in the U.S. and Canada. Grantees design and lead inclusive volunteer service projects that engage 25 to 50+ diverse peers in strengthening community connections during Global Youth Service Day (GYSD) each spring.
Evaluation_Criteria: Youth-led design, engagement of 25-50+ diverse peer volunteers, local community impact
Ideal_Candidate: Youth organizer in the U.S. or Canada mobilizing large peer volunteer groups for community service

Name: Jacobson Institute Innovator Competition
Description: Hosted by the University of Iowa's John Pappajohn Entrepreneurial Center and Jacobson Institute, this annual pitch competition invites U.S. high school inventors to submit an executive summary, business model, and prototype documentation. Selected finalists present live before entrepreneurial judges to compete for cash awards, startup feedback, and statewide or national recognition.
Evaluation_Criteria: Product innovation, business model viability, market research, live pitch quality
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. high school inventor pairing a working prototype with a commercial startup plan

Name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
Description: Founded in 2001 by author T. A. Barron and administered by the Young Heroes Project, the Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes celebrates 25 public-spirited young leaders aged 8–18 across the U.S. and Canada who have led high-impact service or environmental initiatives. Top winners receive $10,000 to support higher education or project expansion alongside national media visibility and peer-network recognition.
Evaluation_Criteria: Heroic initiative, sustained measurable impact, moral leadership, independent drive
Ideal_Candidate: High-impact U.S. or Canadian youth leader who founded a major service or environmental initiative

Name: Diller Teen Tikkun Olam Awards
Description: Presented since 2007 by the Helen Diller Family Foundation, this prestigious award honors up to 15 U.S. Jewish teens annually with $36,000 each—usable toward higher education or their philanthropic initiative—for leading volunteer projects that embody the value of tikkun olam (repairing the world). Recipients also join an active alumni network and attend a celebratory recognition weekend in San Francisco.
Evaluation_Criteria: Entrepreneurial leadership, tikkun olam values, measurable community outcomes, autonomy
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. Jewish teenager serving as the primary leader of a high-impact community service venture

Name: Bezos Scholars Program
Description: The Bezos Scholars Program is a yearlong, tuition-free leadership incubator run by the Bezos Family Foundation for U.S. public high school juniors from Title I or qualifying schools (30%+ free/reduced lunch), alongside African Leadership Academy scholars and nominated educators. Scholars attend an all-expenses-paid week at the Aspen Ideas Festival, receive 1-on-1 college advising and leadership coaching, and receive $1,000 renewable seed grants to launch local Community Change Projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic rigor (3.0+ GPA, advanced coursework), leadership potential, community vision
Ideal_Candidate: Public high school junior from a Title I or qualifying U.S. school with strong civic ambition

Name: Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition (Stiftung Entrepreneurship)
Description: Co-initiated by Stiftung Entrepreneurship (Berlin), the Goi Peace Foundation, and UNESCO, this free global online contest invites young innovators aged 13–29 to complete interactive entrepreneurship training modules and submit original ideas or active enterprises aligned with the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Entries undergo public community engagement and expert jury review to earn international awards and visibility.
Evaluation_Criteria: SDG alignment, entrepreneurial creativity, community engagement, online training completion
Ideal_Candidate: Young social entrepreneur seeking international recognition and online business training

Name: World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council
Description: Coordinated by The Ocean Project since 2016, the World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council selects 20–25 young ocean and climate leaders aged 16–25 from around the world for a one-year virtual term. Council members participate in monthly strategy sessions, receive leadership training, and help shape annual World Ocean Day (June 8) advocacy themes and youth conservation campaigns across nearly 200 countries.
Evaluation_Criteria: Conservation track record, advocacy experience, global collaboration, English fluency
Ideal_Candidate: Passionate marine conservationist or climate advocate with prior grassroots organizing experience

Name: Project Green Challenge
Description: Organized each October by Turning Green, Project Green Challenge (PGC) is a global 30-day sustainability competition engaging high school and college students through daily themed eco-challenges released each morning over 24-hour cycles. Top-performing participants advance as finalists to an all-expenses-paid San Francisco summit, where they pitch original Climate Action Projects for mentorship and the $5,000 Green Award.
Evaluation_Criteria: Daily challenge consistency, creative eco-advocacy, Climate Action Project feasibility
Ideal_Candidate: High school or college student eager to mobilize campus sustainability through daily challenges

Name: Spellman HV Clean Tech Competition
Description: Managed by the Center for Science Teaching & Learning (CSTL) and sponsored by Spellman High Voltage Electronics, this international two-round STEM research and design competition challenges teams of 1–3 students aged 15–18 to solve sustainability crises through clean technology. Round 1 evaluates formal 5–15 page research papers, while finalists build physical prototypes and compete for over $20,000 in cash prizes and awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific research paper quality, clean-tech prototype feasibility, environmental impact
Ideal_Candidate: High school STEM team designing and prototyping hardware or chemical solutions for sustainability

Name: ClimateScience Olympiad (CSO)
Description: Organized by UK-based charity ClimateScience, the ClimateScience Olympiad is a free global online problem-solving competition for youth up to age 25 competing solo or in pairs across <16, 17–20, and 21–25 age brackets. Competitors progress through Qualifiers, Quarter-Finals, a 3-hour Semi-Finals policy essay, and a 3,000-word Finals proposal and presentation for a $15,000 prize pool and UN COP appearances.
Evaluation_Criteria: Systems-level climate analysis, policy and scientific reasoning, structured essay defense
Ideal_Candidate: Analytical student passionate about climate policy, decarbonization, and evidence-based problem solving

Name: COY (UNFCCC Conference of Youth) & YOUNGO Working Groups
Description: Organized by YOUNGO, the official children and youth constituency of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Conference of Youth (COY) convenes young climate leaders at national LCOYs and the global COY immediately preceding each UN COP. Participants collaborate in thematic policy working groups, co-author the Global Youth Statement, and feed youth policy recommendations directly into UN climate negotiations.
Evaluation_Criteria: Climate policy engagement, LCOY/working group participation, advocacy track record
Ideal_Candidate: Youth climate policy advocate seeking direct participation in UNFCCC negotiations and working groups

Name: Trust for Sustainable Living (TSL) International Student Competition
Description: Hosted by the UK educational charity Trust for Sustainable Living, this annual international contest invites primary (ages 7–11) and secondary (ages 12–18) students via registered Teacher Champions to submit original essays or creative video responses on an annual sustainability theme. Top performers worldwide qualify for the online TSL International Student Debates in July and compete for cash awards including a £1,000 Grand Prize.
Evaluation_Criteria: Originality of perspective, clarity of sustainability argument, creative presentation
Ideal_Candidate: Articulate school student able to connect global sustainability themes to local solutions

Name: President's Environmental Youth Award (PEYA)
Description: Established by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 1971, PEYA recognizes K–12 individuals and school clubs across all 10 EPA regions for designing and executing impactful, community-based environmental stewardship projects with an adult sponsor. Regional winners are honored nationally for ecological innovation, measurable environmental outcomes, and public outreach.
Evaluation_Criteria: Environmental stewardship impact, project innovation, community outreach, adult sponsorship
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. K-12 student or club with a documented, teacher-sponsored environmental conservation project

Name: Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT)
Description: Founded in 1998 and run biannually by Harvard and MIT undergraduates, HMMT is one of the world's premier high school math competitions, drawing roughly 1,000 top students per event (November at Harvard for teams of 4–6; February at MIT for teams of 6–8). Competitors tackle individual subject tests, a collaborative proof-based Team Round, and an 80-minute fast-paced Guts Round.
Evaluation_Criteria: Olympiad-level problem solving, speed, proof rigor, team coordination
Ideal_Candidate: Elite high school mathematician (AIME/USAMO caliber) competing at international tournament level

Name: Stanford Math Tournament (SMT)
Description: Hosted every spring by Stanford University undergraduates, SMT brings together high school competitors worldwide across both on-campus and online divisions. Teams compete in a proof-based Power Round, individual topic tests covering Algebra, Calculus, Discrete Math, and Geometry, and a rapid-fire Team/Guts round emphasizing mathematical accuracy and collaborative speed.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical accuracy, speed across subject rounds, team power-round proof writing
Ideal_Candidate: Strong high school competition mathematician comfortable with advanced algebra, combinatorics, and proofs

Name: Berkeley Math Tournament (BMT)
Description: Organized each fall by UC Berkeley's undergraduate math community with in-person and virtual divisions, BMT challenges high school teams from across the U.S. and abroad through rigorous problem-solving rounds. The format blends a collaborative proof-writing Power Round, Individual Focus and General tests across core Olympiad subfields, and a high-speed Team/Relay round.
Evaluation_Criteria: Subject mastery, relay speed, proof clarity, collaborative team strategy
Ideal_Candidate: High school math team seeking rigorous college-hosted fall competition experience

Name: Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition (CMIMC)
Description: An annual winter tournament run by Carnegie Mellon University undergraduates that uniquely pairs Olympiad-level high school mathematics with algorithmic and AI optimization challenges. Alongside Individual, Team, and Power math rounds, teams compete in computer science optimization tasks requiring creative heuristics, combinatorics, and rapid code execution.
Evaluation_Criteria: Algorithmic optimization, mathematical creativity, team power-round rigor
Ideal_Candidate: Hybrid math-and-CS high schooler skilled in combinatorics, programming, and optimization

Name: Caltech Harvey Mudd Math Competition (CHMMC)
Description: Jointly organized each fall by undergraduates at Caltech and Harvey Mudd College (with on-campus and online participation options), CHMMC is a team-focused high school mathematics tournament celebrating creative proof-writing and collaborative inquiry. Teams compete across Individual, Team, and proof-intensive Power rounds, plus tiebreakers designed to stretch Olympiad-style reasoning.
Evaluation_Criteria: Proof creativity, algebraic and geometric rigor, team collaboration
Ideal_Candidate: High school math team strong in proof-based Olympiad problem solving

Name: Duke Math Meet (DMM)
Description: Hosted annually each fall on campus at Duke University, the Duke Math Meet is a regional high school tournament drawing top math clubs across the Southeastern United States. Teams compete across a collaborative Power Round, Individual tests, a Team Round, a fast-paced Relay Round, and a Devil Round that reward precision and proof structure.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical precision, team relay speed, power-round proof structure
Ideal_Candidate: Southeastern U.S. high school math team preparing for national Olympiad circuits

Name: Johns Hopkins Math Tournament (JHMT)
Description: Organized each winter by Johns Hopkins University undergraduates across both on-campus Baltimore and virtual tracks, JHMT hosts dedicated high school and middle school divisions. Competitors tackle Individual subject exams (Algebra, Geometry, Probability, Calculus/Number Theory), a collaborative Team Round, and a fast-paced proof or Guts-style round.
Evaluation_Criteria: Individual accuracy, team round strategy, proof-writing clarity
Ideal_Candidate: High school math competitor looking for competitive East Coast/virtual team rounds

Name: Rice Math Tournament (RMT)
Description: Hosted every spring by the Rice University Mathematics Club in Houston and online, RMT challenges high school teams across individual and collaborative competition formats. Students test their speed and cross-topic intuition across General and Theme individual rounds, a Team Round, and a live-scored Guts Round.
Evaluation_Criteria: Speed, creative problem solving across themed rounds, team accuracy
