Ideal_Candidate: High school math team strong in rapid problem solving and cross-topic intuition

Name: MMATHS Yale
Description: Founded at Yale University and operated simultaneously across multiple major university host sites each fall, Math Majors of America Tournament for High Schools (MMATHS) serves Grades 7–12 teams of up to six students. Competitors complete Individual rounds, a Team Round, a Mixer round, and a high-pressure Lightning Finals buzzer round.
Evaluation_Criteria: Individual mastery, team problem solving, high-pressure lightning buzzer speed
Ideal_Candidate: Grades 7-12 math team eager to compete at regional university hubs including Yale

Name: High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling
Description: Administered annually by COMAP, HiMCM challenges same-school teams of up to four high school students (with a faculty advisor) over a 14-day fall window to model one of two open-ended real-world problems. Teams submit a formal technical paper up to 25 pages detailing assumptions, mathematical derivations, and validation, with top Outstanding U.S. teams advancing to IM2C.
Evaluation_Criteria: Model assumptions, mathematical rigor, data validation, technical paper exposition
Ideal_Candidate: Applied-math and coding team skilled in differential equations, statistics, and LaTeX

Name: Euclid Mathematics Contest
Description: Administered worldwide each spring by the University of Waterloo's Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), the Euclid Contest is a 2.5-hour written exam for senior secondary students. Featuring 10 multi-part short-answer and full-solution proof problems, top scores earn Honour Roll distinctions and are strongly valued for Waterloo mathematics and engineering admissions and scholarships.
Evaluation_Criteria: Full-solution proof clarity, algebraic/geometric insight, rigorous justification
Ideal_Candidate: Grade 12 or senior secondary student aiming for top Waterloo STEM admissions and distinctions

Name: Singapore and Asian Schools Math Olympiad (SASMO)
Description: One of Asia's largest school mathematics competitions for Grades 1–12, SASMO emphasizes non-routine heuristic reasoning, spatial logic, and creative problem solving over rote calculation through a 90-minute individual paper. High-scoring medalists (top ~40% receive certificates/medals) earn invitations to advanced international rounds including SIMOC and IJMO.
Evaluation_Criteria: Non-routine heuristic reasoning, logical deduction, calculation accuracy
Ideal_Candidate: Primary through high school student in Asia seeking Olympiad-style problem exposure

Name: Purple Comet! Math Meet
Description: Purple Comet! Math Meet is a free, annual international online team mathematics competition welcoming middle and high school teams of up to six students worldwide. During a 10-day April contest window, teams choose a fixed timed session (60 minutes for middle school, 90 minutes for high school) to collaboratively solve 20–30 challenging Olympiad-style short-answer problems.
Evaluation_Criteria: Team speed, problem-solving accuracy, collaboration across Olympiad subfields
Ideal_Candidate: School math club or peer group wanting a free, fast-paced international online contest

Name: National Internet Math Olympiad (NIMO)
Description: NIMO is a historically student-run, free online mathematics contest via internetolympiad.org renowned for Olympiad-caliber short-answer problems across seasonal individual and team rounds for middle and high schoolers. While active administration of the contest has been archived, its extensive archive of challenging past problem sets and solutions remains widely used by competition math students for self-study.
Evaluation_Criteria: Short-answer mathematical precision, creative Olympiad techniques
Ideal_Candidate: Self-studying competition math student practicing archived Olympiad-level problem sets

Name: Alibaba Global Mathematics Competition
Description: Launched in 2018 by Alibaba DAMO Academy, this open-entry global online contest attracts tens of thousands of participants worldwide across an open-book Preliminary Round and a proctored Final Round spanning five pure/applied math tracks plus an AI math track. Top finalists compete for substantial cash awards—including $30,000 Gold prizes—with no age or credential barriers.
Evaluation_Criteria: Advanced pure and applied math mastery across proof-based tracks
Ideal_Candidate: Prodigious self-taught mathematician or university-level Olympiad medalist

Name: International Youth Math Challenge (IYMC)
Description: IYMC is an annual international online mathematics competition for high school and university students aged 13–25 designed to encourage creative problem solving beyond school syllabi. Participants advance through three stages—Qualification Round, Pre-Final Round, and a supervised Final Exam—solving proof-based problems for official certificates, special honors, and cash prizes.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical creativity, written solution clarity, analytical persistence
Ideal_Candidate: High school or early college student looking for an accessible international online math contest

Name: Bebras Computational Thinking Challenge
Description: Operating across more than 70 countries, the Bebras Computational Thinking Challenge introduces students aged 6–18 to informatics and algorithmic logic through short, language-independent puzzles that require zero prior coding syntax. Graded across age divisions during annual November school windows, tasks evaluate pattern recognition, abstraction, task decomposition, and logical deduction.
Evaluation_Criteria: Pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithmic decomposition, logical speed
Ideal_Candidate: K-12 student testing innate computational thinking before advanced coding Olympiads

Name: Physics Cup (TalTech)
Description: Founded and led by Prof. Jaan Kalda at Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Physics Cup is an elite international online competition drawing competitors from roughly 90 countries in pre-university and university divisions. Five IPhO/EuPhO+-caliber theoretical problems are released monthly across the season with weekly hints, awarding speed bonuses to solvers who crack them earliest.
Evaluation_Criteria: Theoretical physics ingenuity, mathematical rigor, submission speed before hints
Ideal_Candidate: IPhO/APhO-caliber high school or university physicist thriving on ultra-hard open theoretical problems

Name: Sir Isaac Newton (SIN) Exam (University of Waterloo)
Description: Administered annually by the University of Waterloo's Department of Physics & Astronomy, the Sir Isaac Newton (SIN) Exam is a demanding two-hour physics test open to senior high school students globally. Centered on creative mechanics, kinematics, and energy problems rather than rote formula recall, top scorers earn distinctions and scholarship consideration at Waterloo.
Evaluation_Criteria: Conceptual physics insight, mechanics problem solving, creative derivations
Ideal_Candidate: Grade 12 or AP/IB physics student preparing for top Canadian or global STEM admissions

Name: BPhO Computational Physics Challenge
Description: Part of the British Physics Olympiad suite, the Computational Physics Challenge invites individual or paired secondary students to build numerical simulations, visual plots, and animations based on an annual mathematical-physics specification (such as optics or orbital mechanics). Entrants submit their simulation code alongside a maximum three-minute screencast demonstrating their models and original extensions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Numerical simulation accuracy, physics modeling, code clarity, scientific exposition
Ideal_Candidate: Physics-and-programming student comfortable simulating optics, mechanics, or orbital dynamics

Name: ESA CanSat Competition
Description: Organized by the European Space Agency (ESA) across member and associate states (and Canada), the CanSat Competition challenges student teams aged 14–19 to design, solder, and program a functional mini-satellite fitting inside a standard 330 ml soda-can volume. CanSats are launched by rocket or drone to roughly 1 km altitude to transmit live radio telemetry and execute primary and secondary science missions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Radio telemetry reliability, sensor integration, secondary science mission, flight analysis
Ideal_Candidate: European or Canadian aerospace-minded hardware/software team building embedded flight systems

Name: International Space Settlement Design Competition (ISSDC)
Description: ISSDC is an intensive aerospace engineering simulation in which international high school teams act as competing contractor companies responding to an industry-grade Request for Proposal (RFP) to design orbital or lunar human settlements. Qualifying through regional competitions, finalist alliances convene at NASA's Kennedy Space Center to refine structural, life-support, and automation blueprints before expert aerospace judges.
Evaluation_Criteria: Systems engineering integration, structural/life-support feasibility, RFP compliance, briefing
Ideal_Candidate: Collaborative STEM team excited by orbital architecture, aerospace engineering, and technical proposals

Name: Yale Physics Olympics (YPO)
Description: Hosted annually each fall on campus by the Yale University Physics Department, the Yale Physics Olympics brings four-student high school teams together for a full-day pentathlon of experimental and engineering events. Teams rotate through five timed challenges—ranging from pre-built apparatus and hands-on lab measurements to a Fermi order-of-magnitude estimation quiz—under strict accuracy and collaboration rules.
Evaluation_Criteria: Experimental precision, rapid prototyping, Fermi estimation, team synchronization
Ideal_Candidate: Northeastern U.S. high school physics team skilled in hands-on lab apparatus and estimation

Name: Western Kentucky University (WKU) Physics Olympics
Description: Hosted each winter by Western Kentucky University's Department of Physics and Astronomy, this half-day regional pentathlon challenges four-student high school teams across five themed hands-on physics events. Competitions blend pre-built mechanical devices, impromptu engineering builds, experimental communication tasks, and an order-of-magnitude Fermi estimation quiz.
Evaluation_Criteria: Device performance, order-of-magnitude accuracy, technical teamwork
Ideal_Candidate: Regional U.S. high school physics club testing hands-on engineering builds and estimation

Name: McMaster University / Ontario Physics Olympics (OAPT)
Description: Encompassing the Ontario Association of Physics Teachers (OAPT) Grade 11/12 Physics Contest and McMaster University's annual Physics Olympics, this program tests conceptual physics mastery and practical engineering agility. Individual contestants benchmark curriculum and problem-solving depth on written tests, while school teams compete in hands-on lab and device-building events.
Evaluation_Criteria: Conceptual physics mastery, problem-solving speed, curriculum depth
Ideal_Candidate: Canadian or international high school physics student benchmarking conceptual proficiency

Name: Singapore Physics League (SPhL)
Description: Supported by the Institute of Physics Singapore (IPS), MOE Singapore, and SUTD, the Singapore Physics League is a fast-paced four-hour online team competition for squads of 3–5 secondary and pre-university students across Junior and Senior categories. Teams collaborate in real time on a gamified platform to unlock and solve multi-tier creative physics problems.
Evaluation_Criteria: Speed, physics problem-solving versatility, collaborative strategy across difficulty tiers
Ideal_Candidate: Team of physics Olympiad enthusiasts enjoying real-time gamified collaborative problem solving

Name: S.-T. Yau High School Science Award
Description: Founded in 2008 by Fields Medalist Prof. Shing-Tung Yau and organized by Tsinghua University's Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, this premier research competition evaluates formal, university-grade independent papers written by high school individuals or teams. Entrants compete across Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, and Economic & Financial Modeling, advancing through regional reviews to international oral defense finals.
Evaluation_Criteria: Original theoretical or experimental contribution, academic paper rigor, oral defense
Ideal_Candidate: Advanced high school researcher producing university-grade monographs in math or sciences

Name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
Description: Administered by the Davidson Institute since 2001, the Davidson Fellows Scholarship awards major academic scholarships ($25,000 to $100,000 in recent cycles, historically $10,000 to $50,000) to U.S. citizens and permanent residents aged 18 or younger who have completed a graduate-level original project. Submissions spanning STEM, Literature, Music, Philosophy, or Outside the Box require expert external validation and culminate in a Washington, D.C. reception.
Evaluation_Criteria: Depth of original achievement, expert external validation, societal/academic significance
Ideal_Candidate: Prodigious U.S. student under 18 with a completed, peer-reviewed or patentable body of work

Name: CASTIC
Description: The China Adolescents Science & Technology Innovation Contest (CASTIC, officially the National Youth Science and Technology Innovation Competition) is China's largest pre-college research fair. Convening roughly 500 provincial student winners alongside invited international delegations, finalists showcase original research projects, undergo rigorous technical interviews with expert panels, and compete for national medals and special awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Experimental originality, engineering utility, scientific rigor, defense before judges
Ideal_Candidate: National science-fair winner in China or an invited international STEM delegation

Name: Taiwan International Science Fair
Description: Hosted annually in Taipei by the National Taiwan Science Education Center (NTSEC), the Taiwan International Science Fair (TISF) brings together top Taiwanese high school researchers and international affiliate-fair winners across 13 STEM categories. Delegates present physical research posters, defend experimental reproducibility before international scientist juries, and engage in cross-cultural scientific exchange.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific methodology, experimental reproducibility, international panel oral defense
Ideal_Candidate: High-achieving high school researcher nominated via national science fairs

Name: NSS Gerard K. O'Neill Space Settlement Contest
Description: Run annually by the National Space Society (NSS), this global engineering and design contest invites students up to Grade 12 (solo or in teams) to architect permanent orbital space settlements. Entrants submit comprehensive technical reports detailing orbital mechanics, structural shielding, closed-loop life support, agriculture, and governance for prizes and International Space Development Conference invitations.
Evaluation_Criteria: Engineering plausibility, orbital mechanics, life-support calculations, visual design
Ideal_Candidate: Individual or team of space enthusiasts blending aerospace physics with habitat design

Name: NASA TechRise Student Challenge
Description: Sponsored by NASA and administered with Future Engineers, the NASA TechRise Student Challenge invites U.S. school teams in Grades 6–12 (led by an educator) to design science and technology experiments for high-altitude balloons or suborbital flight tests. Selected winning teams receive $1,500 build grants, standardized flight hardware boxes, and NASA technical mentorship to construct real flight payloads.
Evaluation_Criteria: Experimental feasibility, payload mass/power compliance, scientific merit, educator sponsorship
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. middle or high school STEM team eager to build and fly real atmospheric/suborbital payloads

Name: University of Oxford: Isaac Physics Senior Physics Challenge
Description: Combining the BPhO Senior Physics Challenge for Year 12 / Grade 11 students with the Isaac Science/Physics residential bootcamp, this program pushes high-achieving physicists well beyond standard A-level syllabi. Competitors tackle multi-step calculus, vector mechanics, and experimental reasoning problems, with top UK performers invited to intensive summer physics instruction at Cambridge/Oxford.
Evaluation_Criteria: Multi-step mathematical physics fluency, vector/calculus reasoning, problem-solving persistence
Ideal_Candidate: Year 12 / Grade 11 physics student preparing for UK Olympiads and Oxbridge physics admissions

Name: Harvard-MIT Chemistry Olympiad (HMChO)
Description: Organized each spring by Harvard and MIT undergraduates with both in-person and online tracks, HMChO challenges high school individuals and teams across organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Featuring USNCO-caliber individual subject exams and collaborative team rounds, the tournament tests deep chemical intuition, thermodynamics, and kinetics under competitive time limits.
Evaluation_Criteria: Advanced chemical intuition, thermodynamics/kinetics speed, team collaborative scoring
Ideal_Candidate: High school chemistry student (USNCO-caliber) seeking university-hosted team competition

Name: International Chemistry Quiz (Royal Australian Chemical Institute)
Description: Organized by the Royal Australian Chemical Institute (RACI), the International Chemistry Quiz (ICQ) engages tens of thousands of secondary students across more than 20 countries each year. Its 30-question conceptual exam emphasizes chemical literacy, experimental reasoning, and deducing patterns from unfamiliar data rather than syllabus memorization, awarding High Distinction, Distinction, and Excellence certificates.
Evaluation_Criteria: Chemical literacy, deductive reasoning from unfamiliar data, problem-solving accuracy
Ideal_Candidate: Secondary school student worldwide testing conceptual and analytical chemistry aptitude

Name: Cambridge Chemistry Challenge (C3L6)
Description: Organized by the University of Cambridge Department of Chemistry and co-sponsored by St Catharine's College, C3L6 is a demanding 90-minute written exam for Year 12 / Lower Sixth (and international Grade 11) students stretching beyond standard syllabi. Featuring extended real-world chemistry problems, it awards Copper, Silver, Gold, and top ~0.5% Roentgenium honors (with UK Roentgenium winners invited to a Cambridge residential camp).
Evaluation_Criteria: Chemical deduction, unfamiliar organic/physical mechanism analysis, mathematical rigor
Ideal_Candidate: Ambitious Year 12 / Grade 11 chemistry student preparing for IChO selection or Oxbridge Natural Sciences

Name: Chem 13 News Exam (University of Waterloo)
Description: Administered online each spring by the University of Waterloo's Department of Chemistry, the Chem 13 News Exam is a 75-minute multiple-choice test designed for senior high school chemistry students globally. Covering advanced general, equilibrium, thermodynamic, kinetic, and organic chemistry topics, top scorers earn certificates, magazine recognition, and Waterloo scholarship consideration.
Evaluation_Criteria: Quantitative chemical accuracy, equilibrium/thermo speed, conceptual breadth
Ideal_Candidate: Senior high school or AP/IB Chemistry student benchmarking skills internationally

Name: Washington University Chemistry Tournament (WUCT)
Description: Created and run by Washington University in St. Louis undergraduates, WUCT is a one-day spring tournament uniting six-student U.S. high school teams on campus. Competitors tackle Individual exams, specialized Topic rounds, and fast-paced collaborative Team/Relay rounds designed to reward creative interdisciplinary applications of chemistry.
Evaluation_Criteria: Individual mastery, creative interdisciplinary chemistry applications, team strategy
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. high school chemistry team combining deep subject knowledge with collaborative problem solving

Name: Berkeley Chemistry Tournament (BCT)
Description: Hosted each spring by UC Berkeley undergraduates across in-person and online divisions, BCT challenges high school teams across theoretical and applied chemistry. Teams compete in Individual tests, a collaborative Team Round, and fast-paced Relay/Tiebreaker rounds spanning organic mechanisms, physical chemistry, and analytical problem solving.
Evaluation_Criteria: Analytical speed, organic/inorganic depth, collaborative round coordination
Ideal_Candidate: High school chemistry team interested in competitive university-run science tournaments

Name: ChemiCo
Description: Part of the Singapore-based StemCo International Science Competitions reaching students across 40+ countries, ChemiCo is a seasonal 90-minute online exam testing logical and analytical mastery of chemistry. Rather than testing rote definitions, questions focus on applying stoichiometry, bonding, reaction mechanisms, and experimental data reasoning across grade-level divisions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Logical application of stoichiometry, bonding, reactions, and experimental reasoning
Ideal_Candidate: School student globally seeking seasonal, application-focused online chemistry testing

Name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
Description: Sponsored by the U.S. Department of Defense and administered with the National Science Teaching Association (NSTA), JSHS engages thousands of U.S. high schoolers in Grades 9–12 across 49 regional symposia. Students submit and orally defend original STEM research papers, with regional top finishers advancing expenses-paid to Nationals to compete for up to $12,000 in undergraduate scholarships and cash awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific originality, experimental design, written paper rigor, oral/poster defense
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. high school researcher with a completed, independent STEM research manuscript

Name: Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) Schools' Analyst Competition
Description: Run annually by the Royal Society of Chemistry for Year 12 / Lower Sixth teams of three across the UK and Ireland, the Schools' Analyst Competition tests practical wet-lab precision and analytical deduction. Teams perform hands-on titrations, chromatography, and spectroscopy-based problem solving in school and regional heats to qualify for the UK/Ireland Final.
Evaluation_Criteria: Wet-lab precision, analytical deduction, teamwork, safety compliance
Ideal_Candidate: UK or Irish Year 12 chemistry team skilled in hands-on analytical laboratory techniques

Name: International Research Olympiad
Description: Organized by the Samyak Science Society across 89+ countries, the International Research Olympiad (IRO) tests scientific paper literacy, statistical data interpretation, and experimental design rather than memorized facts. Students advance from online Opens through virtual Semifinals (top ~10%) to in-person Finals hosted at Harvard University for international medals.
Evaluation_Criteria: Literature synthesis, statistical data interpretation, experimental inquiry design
Ideal_Candidate: High school student adept at reading peer-reviewed papers and critiquing experimental methodology

Name: International Biology Bowl
Description: The International Biology Bowl is an annual global online team competition for high schoolers combining written qualifying exams with bracketed, fast-paced live buzzer elimination rounds. Teams divide sub-disciplines across molecular biology, genetics, cell physiology, and ecology to answer Olympiad-level conceptual and rapid-recall questions under head-to-head match pressure.
Evaluation_Criteria: Biological breadth, buzzer recall speed, team division of sub-disciplines
Ideal_Candidate: High school biology team strong in rapid-recall trivia and Olympiad-style concepts

Name: British Biology Olympiad
Description: Organized by UK Biology Competitions and the Royal Society of Biology for post-16 students, the British Biology Olympiad challenges competitors through two 45-minute online papers covering cellular biology, genetics, physiology, and ecology. Medal winners earn Gold, Silver, or Bronze honors, and top UK scorers advance toward International Biology Olympiad (IBO) team selection.
Evaluation_Criteria: Cellular/molecular intuition, genetics, ecology, unfamiliar biological data analysis
Ideal_Candidate: Year 12/13 biology student aiming for gold medals or UK IBO national team selection

Name: USABO Open Exam
Description: Administered by the Center for Excellence in Education (CEE), the USA Biolympiad (USABO) Open Exam is a 50-minute multiple-choice test serving as the first qualifying stage for U.S. high schoolers. Top scorers advance to the Semifinal Exam, the intensive National Finals training camp, and ultimately selection to represent Team USA at the International Biology Olympiad (IBO).
Evaluation_Criteria: Advanced Campbell-level biology mastery, experimental reasoning, speed
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. high school biology standout aiming for Semifinals, National Finals camp, and IBO

Name: University of Toronto National Biology Competition
Description: Hosted annually online by the University of Toronto's Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology and Cell & Systems Biology, this 75-minute multiple-choice exam benchmarks senior high school students across Canada and internationally. Testing biochemistry, physiology, genetics, and evolution, top scorers earn National Biology Scholar honors and top-percentile awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Biochemistry, physiology, genetics, and evolution analytical reasoning
Ideal_Candidate: Senior high school or AP/IB Biology student seeking international academic benchmarking

Name: International Brain Bee (Neuroscience)
Description: Founded in 1998 by Dr. Norbert Myslinski, the International Brain Bee is the premier global neuroscience competition engaging tens of thousands of teens aged 13–19 across more than 50 countries. Advancing from local chapters to National Championships and the World Championship, competitors are tested on neuroanatomy, histology, patient diagnosis, and live Q&A mastery.
Evaluation_Criteria: Neuroanatomy, patient diagnosis, histology, neuroscience oral/written mastery
Ideal_Candidate: Teen passionate about neuroscience, neurology, and medicine aiming for national/world finals

Name: iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machine Competition)
Description: Founded at MIT and administered by the iGEM Foundation, iGEM's High School Division challenges multidisciplinary teams with adult instructors to engineer synthetic biology systems using standard biological parts. Over a multi-month cycle, teams execute wet-lab testing, mathematical modeling, and Human Practices outreach before presenting their wiki and research at the Grand Jamboree for medals and Grand Prizes.
Evaluation_Criteria: Wet-lab synthetic biology execution, mathematical modeling, human practices, wiki/presentation
Ideal_Candidate: High school team with lab mentorship building engineered biological devices and public outreach

Name: International BioGENEius Challenge
Description: Hosted by the Biotechnology Institute, the International BioGENEius Challenge recognizes high school researchers (Grades 9–12) presenting original biotechnology innovations across Global Healthcare, Sustainability, and Environment tracks. Advancing from regional, national, and virtual qualifiers, finalists defend their wet-lab methodology and translational impact before industry and academic experts at the BIO International Convention.
Evaluation_Criteria: Biotech novelty, rigorous lab methodology, translational/commercial potential
Ideal_Candidate: High school bioengineer or wet-lab researcher with applied clinical or agricultural research

Name: National High School Model United Nations (NHSMUN)
Description: Organized each March in New York City by IMUNA, NHSMUN is the world's largest and most internationally diverse Model UN conference for high school students. Thousands of delegates debate global policy across specialized UN organs using consensus-focused rules, culminating in closing plenary sessions held inside the United Nations Headquarters.
Evaluation_Criteria: Diplomatic consensus-building, UN procedure mastery, position paper depth, resolution drafting
Ideal_Candidate: High school MUN delegation seeking large-scale diplomatic simulation at UN Headquarters

Name: The Hague International Model United Nations (THIMUN)
Description: Founded in 1968, THIMUN is a flagship five-day international Model UN conference held every January at the World Forum in The Hague, Netherlands. Convening over 3,000 secondary delegates from dozens of countries, the conference emphasizes formal lobbying, clause-by-clause resolution drafting, and consensus-driven diplomacy under official THIMUN procedure.
Evaluation_Criteria: Lobbying, clause-by-clause resolution drafting, international policy accuracy, public speaking
Ideal_Candidate: Experienced international school delegation proficient in consensus-style MUN diplomacy

Name: Harvard Model United Nations (HMUN)
Description: Hosted annually each January in Boston by Harvard University's International Relations Council, HMUN brings together over 4,000 high school delegates from across the globe for North American-style committee debate. Spanning General Assemblies, ECOSOCs, specialized agencies, and fast-paced crisis committees, HMUN is widely regarded as a benchmark for competitive MUN diplomacy and bloc leadership.
Evaluation_Criteria: Rhetorical command, coalition leadership, policy research, fast-paced crisis adaptability
Ideal_Candidate: Competitive high school delegate or school delegation aiming for Best Delegate honors in Boston

Name: THIMUN Qatar
Description: Hosted annually in Doha as a premier regional affiliate of the THIMUN Foundation, THIMUN Qatar unites over a thousand Middle Eastern and international high school students for four days of UN-style debate. Delegates engage in structured lobbying, resolution authoring, and cross-cultural diplomacy across General Assemblies, Security Council, and specialized forums.
Evaluation_Criteria: Resolution authoring, cross-cultural diplomacy, research depth, procedural decorum
Ideal_Candidate: High school MUN delegate in MENA or international schools experienced in THIMUN rules

Name: Yale Model United Nations
Description: Hosted every January on Yale University's campus in New Haven by the Yale International Relations Association, YMUN is one of North America's oldest and most competitive high school MUN conferences. Over 1,500 delegates debate across General Assembly, ECOSOC, regional bodies, and dynamic crisis committees requiring rigorous position papers and bloc leadership.
Evaluation_Criteria: Oratory persuasiveness, position paper rigor, bloc leadership, crisis creativity
Ideal_Candidate: Ambitious high school delegate seeking top-tier Ivy League MUN competition

Name: Ivy League Model United Nations Conference (ILMUNC)
Description: Organized each winter in Philadelphia by the University of Pennsylvania's International Affairs Association, ILMUNC convenes thousands of high school delegates across General Assembly, ECOSOC, specialized, and crisis committees. Known for fast-moving East Coast North American procedure, ILMUNC emphasizes sharp debate, detailed resolution drafting, and collaborative crisis negotiation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Debate incisiveness, resolution quality, collaborative negotiation, crisis responsiveness
Ideal_Candidate: High school MUN team thriving on fast-moving U.S. East Coast committee debate

Name: North American Invitational Model United Nations (NAIMUN)
Description: Hosted every February in Washington, D.C. by Georgetown University's International Relations Association, NAIMUN draws over 3,000 high school delegates for ultra-competitive foreign policy, national security, and crisis simulations. Renowned for D.C. embassy briefings and expert staff, the conference rewards geopolitical accuracy, directive writing, and sustained diplomatic leadership.
Evaluation_Criteria: Geopolitical accuracy, diplomatic tact, directive writing, sustained committee leadership
Ideal_Candidate: Top-circuit high school MUN delegate focused on foreign policy and international security

Name: Berkeley Model United Nations (BMUN)
Description: Founded in 1952 as the world's oldest Model UN conference, BMUN is hosted annually in March on the UC Berkeley campus for more than 1,500 high school delegates. Emphasizing substantive policy research, inclusive diplomacy, and collaborative resolution building across novice to advanced committees, BMUN anchors the U.S. West Coast collegiate-run MUN circuit.
Evaluation_Criteria: Substantive policy research, collaborative resolution building, speaking clarity
Ideal_Candidate: High school delegation seeking historic, research-intensive West Coast MUN competition

Name: Columbia Model United Nations Conference and Exposition (CMUNCE)
Description: Hosted every January at Columbia University in New York City by the Columbia International Relations Council and Association, CMUNCE specializes exclusively in small, high-intensity crisis committees and historical simulations rather than traditional large General Assemblies. Delegates thrive on rapid backroom directive execution, improvised strategic negotiation, and dynamic crisis arcs.
Evaluation_Criteria: Crisis arc innovation, rapid directive execution, strategic negotiation, theatrical poise
Ideal_Candidate: Experienced crisis-MUN delegate who excels at backroom strategy and improvised problem solving

Name: Stanford Model United Nations Conference (SMUNC)
Description: Hosted each November on Stanford University's campus by the Society for International Affairs at Stanford, SMUNC convenes roughly 800 high school delegates across traditional, specialized, and crisis committees. Frequently spotlighting emerging technology policy, cyber governance, and international security, the conference emphasizes analytical depth and creative diplomacy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Analytical depth, creative problem solving, persuasive speaking, bloc diplomacy
Ideal_Candidate: High school delegate interested in technology policy, international security, and crisis debate

Name: Vanderbilt Model United Nations (VCMUN)
Description: Hosted annually each spring in Nashville by Vanderbilt University's International Relations Society, VCMUN offers U.S. high school delegations accessible yet competitive General Assembly, specialized, and crisis committees. Delegates are evaluated on thorough position paper research, active floor participation, and constructive coalition building across diverse international topics.
Evaluation_Criteria: Position paper quality, committee participation, collaborative compromise
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. high school MUN club seeking strong collegiate-run Southern circuit competition

Name: UCLA Model United Nations (BruinMUN)
Description: Held every November on the UCLA campus in Los Angeles, BruinMUN is one of the largest fall high school Model UN conferences on the U.S. West Coast. Welcoming more than a thousand delegates across novice, intermediate, advanced, and crisis committees, BruinMUN emphasizes structured parliamentary preparedness, public speaking poise, and collaborative resolution drafting.
Evaluation_Criteria: Preparedness, public speaking poise, resolution structure, diplomatic collaboration
Ideal_Candidate: Novice to advanced high school delegate competing on the California MUN circuit

Name: Princeton Model United Nations Conference (PMUNC)
Description: Organized each November by Princeton University's International Relations Council, PMUNC brings top high school delegations from across the U.S. and abroad together for intensive policy and crisis simulations. Known for rigorous academic background guides and competitive committee rooms, the conference tests concise writing, strategic debate control, and crisis agility.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic research depth, strategic debate control, concise writing, crisis agility
Ideal_Candidate: Competitive high school delegate aiming for fall Ivy League circuit accolades

Name: Dartmouth Model United Nations (DARTMUN)
Description: Hosted each spring at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire, DARTMUN is an intimate, high-engagement high school Model UN conference designed around smaller committee sizes and direct collegiate staff mentorship. Delegates tackle specialized policy and crisis scenarios where close analytical argumentation and collaborative drafting carry significant weight.
Evaluation_Criteria: Committee engagement, analytical argumentation, collaborative drafting
Ideal_Candidate: High school delegate preferring smaller, discussion-rich Ivy League committee rooms

Name: University of Toronto Model United Nations
Description: Held each February in downtown Toronto by University of Toronto students, UTMUN is one of Canada's flagship high school Model UN conferences. Drawing Canadian and international school delegations across General Assembly, specialized, and fast-paced crisis committees, UTMUN rewards diplomatic nuance, policy command, and creative backroom strategy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Diplomatic nuance, policy command, crisis creativity, formal debate skill
Ideal_Candidate: Canadian or international high school MUN delegation competing in North America's winter circuit

Name: Berlin Model United Nations
Description: Founded in 1992 at the John F. Kennedy School in Berlin, BERMUN is an annual four-day THIMUN-affiliated international conference held each November for 700+ secondary students across Europe and beyond. Conducted in English under THIMUN consensus rules, delegates collaborate in themed committees, Security Council, and Special Conferences on European and global policy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Consensus-building, international policy accuracy, English diplomatic fluency
Ideal_Candidate: European or international secondary school student engaged in THIMUN-procedure diplomacy

Name: International Model United Nations of Lubeck
Description: Organized annually each May by students of Thomas-Mann-Schule in Lübeck, Germany, MUNOL is a five-day international conference welcoming over 350 secondary delegates from across Europe. Alongside formal UN-procedure committee debate and resolution drafting, the conference emphasizes deep cross-cultural exchange through local host-family stays.
Evaluation_Criteria: Cross-cultural collaboration, UN-procedure debate, resolution drafting
Ideal_Candidate: High school delegation seeking an immersive week-long European MUN with host-family exchange

Name: Porto International Model United Nations
Description: Hosted each February by CLIP - Oporto International School in Porto, Portugal, Oporto Model United Nations (OPOMUN) convenes more than 250 international high school delegates across nine UN-style committees. Known for welcoming Southern European and global delegations, OPOMUN evaluates topical research, rhetorical clarity, diplomatic decorum, and resolution negotiation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Resolution negotiation, topical research, rhetorical clarity, diplomatic decorum
Ideal_Candidate: European or international secondary student competing in Southern Europe's school MUN circuit

Name: Milan Model United Nations (MILANMUN)
Description: With over two decades of history, MILANMUN is Milan's longest-running high school Model UN conference, hosted each spring by Civico Polo Scolastico Manzoni alongside partner universities in Milan. School delegations from Italy and across Europe collaborate across General Assembly and specialized committees focused on policy research and constructive debate.
Evaluation_Criteria: School-delegation teamwork, policy preparation, constructive committee debate
Ideal_Candidate: High school MUN club in Europe seeking a longstanding spring conference in Italy

Name: CAIMUN (Copenhagen International Model United Nations)
Description: CAIMUN (Canadian International Model United Nations) is a major annual 1,000+ delegate high school conference held every May in Vancouver featuring General Assembly, specialized, and crisis committees. Separately, Copenhagen International School hosts CIMUN in Denmark, offering an analogous international Nordic MUN experience.
Evaluation_Criteria: Crisis adaptability, formal debate eloquence, policy depth, bloc leadership
Ideal_Candidate: High school delegate seeking major North American Pacific-coast or Nordic international MUN experience

Name: Harvard Model United Nations India (HMUN India)
Description: Co-hosted annually in India (historically in Hyderabad/Bengaluru) by Harvard University's International Relations Council and Worldview Education, HMUN India is one of Asia's largest and most prestigious high school MUN conferences. Thousands of delegates from India and across Asia debate before Harvard-student chairs across GAs, specialized agencies, and crisis rooms for Best Delegate honors.
Evaluation_Criteria: Substantive foreign policy mastery, public speaking polish, negotiation impact
Ideal_Candidate: Indian or Asian high school MUN delegate aiming for Harvard-adjudicated Best Delegate awards

Name: Cathedral Model United Nations
Description: Founded in 1996 by The Cathedral and John Connon School in Mumbai, CMUN is India's oldest student-run Model UN conference, convening 700+ delegates each August. Renowned for rigorous parliamentary standards, historic and contemporary crisis simulations, and intense committee debate, CMUN serves as a cornerstone of India's school MUN circuit.
Evaluation_Criteria: Debate rigor, historical/crisis simulation skill, policy preparation, parliamentary skill
Ideal_Candidate: Indian Grades 8-12 delegate seeking India's flagship legacy school MUN circuit

Name: Cairo American College Model United Nations (CACMUN)
Description: Established in 1978 and affiliated with THIMUN, CACMUN is hosted each October at Cairo American College in Egypt, bringing together MENA and international school delegations across 10 diverse committees. Operating under THIMUN consensus procedure, delegates focus on structured lobbying, resolution authoring, and multilateral problem solving.
Evaluation_Criteria: THIMUN-style consensus lobbying, resolution writing, international perspective
Ideal_Candidate: MENA or international school delegate practicing THIMUN diplomacy in Cairo

Name: Ransom Everglades Model United Nations (REMUN)
Description: Hosted each fall in Miami by Ransom Everglades School, REMUN brings together South Florida middle and high school delegations for competitive committee debate across General Assembly, ECOSOC, Human Rights, and Security Council rooms. Designed to build regional tournament readiness, REMUN rewards clear resolution writing, committee engagement, and speaking confidence.
Evaluation_Criteria: Committee participation, resolution clarity, public speaking confidence
Ideal_Candidate: Florida high school MUN delegate building regional tournament experience

Name: Global MUN Turkey (MUNGLOBAL TR)
Description: An annual multi-day residential Model UN conference held in Antalya, Türkiye (typically in November or December), bringing together roughly 500 international high school and university delegates. Conducted in English across standard UN organs and specialized councils, the event pairs formal resolution drafting and diplomacy with cross-cultural networking.
Evaluation_Criteria: Diplomatic speaking, resolution drafting, cross-cultural negotiation
Ideal_Candidate: High school or university delegate seeking an international residential MUN conference in Turkiye

Name: World Schools Debating Championships (WSDC)
Description: Held annually each summer in a rotating host country, WSDC is the pinnacle international championship for high school debating, uniting over 70 official national squads selected through country trials. Teams compete 3-on-3 across eight preliminary rounds and knockouts on both prepared and one-hour impromptu motions, judged on content, style, and strategy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Content rigor, strategic rebuttal, style/delivery, prepared & impromptu adaptability
Ideal_Candidate: National-team high school debater selected through official country trials

Name: NSDA National Tournament (National Speech & Debate Association)
Description: The NSDA National Tournament is the largest academic speech and debate championship in the United States, bringing over 4,000 district qualifiers together every June across Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, World Schools, Congressional Debate, and Speech events. Competitors advance through multi-day preliminary and elimination rounds before national judging panels.
Evaluation_Criteria: Argumentative clash, evidence synthesis, cross-examination, rhetorical polish
Ideal_Candidate: U.S. middle or high school speech and debate competitor qualifying through NSDA districts

Name: International Competition for Young Debaters (ICYD)
Description: Founded by the Oxford Union in 2003 and co-hosted alternately with the Cambridge Union, ICYD is the world's largest junior British Parliamentary (BP) debating championship for students aged 15 and under. Over 1,000 teams enter UK and international regional qualifiers for roughly 48 Finals Day places at Oxford or Cambridge across Open and ESL divisions.
Evaluation_Criteria: BP role fulfillment, rapid 15-minute prep analysis, extension strategy, rebuttal
Ideal_Candidate: Junior secondary debater aged 15 or under excelling in fast-paced British Parliamentary format

Name: International Schools Debating Championships
Description: Hosted by QatarDebate Center in Doha and across hybrid international tracks, ISDC convenes high school teams from dozens of nations to debate pressing global policy issues in World Schools format. Featuring distinct Arabic and English divisions, the championship emphasizes structured logical argumentation, cross-cultural policy fluency, and crisp rebuttal.
Evaluation_Criteria: Logical argumentation, cross-cultural policy awareness, rebuttal clarity
Ideal_Candidate: School debate team competing internationally in World Schools-style English or Arabic debate

Name: European Schools Debating Championship (EuroSDC)
Description: An annual spring regional championship conducted under official WSDC rules, EuroSDC unites European national and development high school squads to debate prepared and impromptu motions on European and global affairs. Serving both as a major regional title and WSDC preparation ground, rounds evaluate matter, manner, and method.
Evaluation_Criteria: Matter, manner, and method under WSDC rules, European policy literacy
Ideal_Candidate: European high school national or development squad preparing for WSDC

Name: Asian World Schools Debating Championship (AWSDC)
Description: AWSDC is a flagship annual international tournament hosted in major Asian hubs such as Bangkok, uniting top national and institutional high school teams across Asia and worldwide under WSDC rules. Teams debate prepared and impromptu motions across preliminary and elimination brackets, serving as both a prestigious championship and premier WSDC prep.
Evaluation_Criteria: WSDC speaker score excellence, strategic whip speeches, impromptu depth
Ideal_Candidate: Top Asian or international school debate team using AWSDC as flagship prep or title target

Name: World Individual Debating and Public Speaking Championships (WIDPSC)
Description: Founded in 1988, WIDPSC is an annual English-language international championship testing individual high school orators representing more than 20 countries. Every competitor participates across four distinct events—Parliamentary Debate, Impromptu Speaking, Interpretive Reading, and a Prepared Persuasive or After-Dinner Speech—vying for individual event titles and the overall World Champion award.
Evaluation_Criteria: Versatility across debate, impromptu, persuasive, and interpretive speaking events
Ideal_Candidate: All-around high school orator skilled in both competitive debate and individual public speaking

Name: DCA National Championship (National Debate Coaches Association)
Description: Organized annually each spring by the National Debate Coaches Association (NDCA), the NDCA National Championship brings together top varsity competitors from NDCA member high schools across the United States. Crowning national champions in Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, and World Schools debate, the tournament tests technical national-circuit argumentation, evidence speed, and judge adaptation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical national-circuit argumentation, evidence speed, judge adaptation
Ideal_Candidate: Competitive U.S. national-circuit debater from an NDCA member high school

Name: Cal Invitational at UC Berkeley
Description: Hosted every February on the UC Berkeley campus, the Cal Invitational is one of the largest and most prestigious high school speech and debate tournaments in the United States. Drawing thousands of competitors across Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, Parliamentary, Congress, and Speech, it serves as a top-tier Tournament of Champions (TOC) bid tournament.
Evaluation_Criteria: TOC-level technical clash, research briefs, cross-examination control
Ideal_Candidate: High school Policy, LD, PF, or Speech competitor chasing Tournament of Champions bids

Name: Stanford Invitational
Description: Held annually each February by Stanford University's Speech and Debate Society across in-person and online divisions, the Stanford Invitational is a flagship U.S. national-circuit tournament. Awarding coveted Tournament of Champions (TOC) bids across Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, Congressional Debate, and Speech, it evaluates rigorous case construction and fast-paced rebuttal.
Evaluation_Criteria: Analytical rigor, case construction, fast-paced rebuttal, TOC-level poise
Ideal_Candidate: Top high school speech and debate competitor targeting national-circuit elimination rounds

Name: Yale Invitational
Description: Hosted each September on the Yale University campus by the Yale Debate Association, the Yale Invitational traditionally opens the U.S. national high school speech and debate circuit each fall. Offering early-season Tournament of Champions (TOC) qualifying bids across Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, Parliamentary, Congress, and Speech, it tests early-season topic mastery.
Evaluation_Criteria: Early-season topic preparation, persuasive delivery, structural clash
Ideal_Candidate: High school debater or speaker launching a national-circuit TOC campaign each fall

Name: Oxford Schools' Debating Competition
Description: Run by the Oxford Union, Oxford Schools' is the UK's largest British Parliamentary debating competition for same-school pairs aged 14–18, attracting over 1,000 students from 350+ schools across UK and international regional qualifiers. Top-ranked pairs advance to Finals Day at the Oxford Union to debate four preliminary rounds and knockouts across Open, Novice, ESL, and State School categories.
Evaluation_Criteria: BP comparative analysis, 15-minute prep strategy, crisp rebuttal, manner
Ideal_Candidate: High school pair mastering British Parliamentary debating and aiming for Oxford Finals

Name: Cambridge Schools Debating Competition
Description: Organized by the Cambridge Union Society, Cambridge Schools is a premier international British Parliamentary tournament for pairs of secondary students aged 14–18. Teams compete through UK and international regional qualifiers during winter before top-ranked pairs advance to Finals Day in Cambridge in March, judged on principled argumentation, comparative extension, and responsive delivery.
Evaluation_Criteria: Principled and practical BP argumentation, strategic responsiveness, clear delivery
Ideal_Candidate: Secondary school debating pair competing in UK or international Cambridge Schools regionals

Name: Emory University Barkley Forum for High Schools
Description: Hosted every January since 1951 at Emory University in Atlanta, the Barkley Forum for High Schools is one of the oldest and most selective national-circuit invitationals in U.S. speech and debate. Drawing over 1,000 competitors from across dozens of states in Policy (Pelham Debates), Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, Congress, and Speech, it awards prestigious Tournament of Champions (TOC) bids.
Evaluation_Criteria: National-circuit research depth, strategic debate framing, persuasive eloquence
Ideal_Candidate: Elite U.S. high school speech and debate competitor seeking prestigious mid-winter TOC bids
